title: Quantifying anisotropic impacts of LCZ landscape patterns on NO2 variabilities in the Yangtze River Delta, China
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Urban landscape patterns strongly affect air quality, yet existing studies often neglect anisotropic processes, rely on arbitrary fixed-radius buffers, and lack standardized classification frameworks. To overcome these limitations, we developed a novel analytical framework that integrates high-accuracy Local Climate Zone (LCZ) classification, multi-scale spatial modeling, and a shape-adaptive influence zone. Central to this framework is the Adaptive Directionally Weighted Sector Influence Zone (ADWSIZ), a new method that explicitly captures the directional heterogeneity of landscape effects on pollutants. Applied to station-based NO 2 measurements in the Yangtze River Delta (YRD) urban agglomeration, we used multi-scale Geographically Weighted Ridge Regression (GWRR) to identify a 4000 m circular buffer as the optimal modeling scale, revealing a clear decoupling from the intrinsic static LCZ pattern scale (approximately 1000 m). Building upon this optimal distance, the ADWSIZ model was developed to refine the influence zone’s shape. The application of ADWSIZ improved model performance (Adjusted R 2 : 0.464 → 0.506 ; RMSE: 2.950 → 2.834 µg/m 3 ) and reduced residual spatial autocorrelation. Our findings highlight that the anisotropic influence of features like industrial land and compact high-rise fabrics is a critical, previously underexplored factor in explaining NO 2 variation. This study establishes a replicable and transferable methodology that advances the conceptualization of influence zones from simple distance-based buffers to scale- and shape-adaptive forms, offering a robust tool for refining spatial coupling analyses between urban morphology and air pollutants.

title: Large-scale building instance segmentation in diverse urban scenes based on LiDAR data
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Building 3D profiles constitute critical factors in urban environmental analyses, including assessments of urban heat island effects, carbon emissions, population distribution, and related challenges. LiDAR data provide comprehensive high-resolution 3D information, enabling the acquisition of detailed 3D building profiles. However, in dense urban environments, buildings are in diverse shapes and heights, and are close to one another, making it challenging to extract building instances. In this paper, we propose BuildGroup, a novel building instance segmentation model for both Airborne Laser Scanning (ALS)-based and Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV) datasets. It employs the progressive learning strategy in the feature aggregation, which uses prior 2D knowledge from the Segment Anything Model (SAM) to infer spatial relationships within point clouds and mitigate cross-source discrepancies. An offset enhancement module is introduced to mitigate the effects of diverse point densities, improving instance clustering by compacting point cloud distributions. Additionally, an edge-enhanced loss function prioritizes boundary point accuracy during training to enhance morphological precision. Furthermore, we present a building LiDAR dataset with instance-level building information, which fills a key gap in real-world, large-scale urban point cloud segmentation, particularly for ALS-based sparse façade data. Experimental results validate the framework’s capability to produce accurate building instance information across varying urban densities. All code and data are available at https://github.com/littlebeen/BuildGroup .

title: An interpretable DM-PINN for retrieving mangrove canopy carbon, nitrogen, and potassium contents using Sentinel-2 and SDGSAT-1 observations along China's southeastern coast
abstract: Mangroves are among the most important blue carbon ecosystems, contributing substantially to global carbon sequestration and biodiversity conservation. Canopy carbon (CCC), nitrogen (CNC), and potassium (CKC) contents provide critical indicators of nutrient cycling, ecosystem functioning, and ecological health. However, the structural complexity and strong spatial heterogeneity of mangroves present major obstacles to understanding the spectral response mechanisms and achieving reliable large-scale retrieval of these biochemical parameters. To address these limitations, we developed an interpretable retrieval framework that integrates causal analysis with physical constraints for reliable estimation of mangrove biochemical parameters. First, we proposed a Multi-Channel Chatterjee-Enhanced Correlation Spectrum Analysis (MC-ξ-CS) method that integrates causal discovery to systematically identify spectral bands causally associated with CCC, CNC, and CKC. For large-scale retrieval of mangrove canopy parameters, the identified causal relationships were transferred to satellite observations through a Global Angle-Divergence Spectral Transfer (GADT) framework, yielding robust estimation (R2 = 0.511–0.669). Subsequently, a Dual-Mechanism Guided Physics-Informed Neural Network (DM-PINN) was developed to synergistically integrate causal analysis and physical constraints, achieving robust retrieval performance (R2 = 0.604–0.83) for three representative mangrove species and enhancing the physical interpretability of the results. To the best of our knowledge, this study provides the first comprehensive large-scale retrieval of key mangrove biochemical parameters along the southeastern coast of China, revealing CCC values of 409.18–566.89 g/kg (C/N = 9.77–14.21), CNC values of 14.38–74.9 g/kg (N/K = 1.99–3.86), and CKC values of 4.78–19.67 g/kg (C/K = 28.22–37.67). Distinct inter-provincial spatial patterns were observed: CNC and CKC exhibited similar gradients, increasing from landward to seaward regions, whereas CCC displayed an opposite spatial distribution pattern with lower values in coastal regions. Moreover, CCC was strongly positively correlated with CNC, while CKC showed negative correlations with both parameters. Collectively, this study established a novel theoretical and methodological framework for elucidating the spectral response mechanisms of mangrove biochemical parameters, offering critical scientific support for large-scale mangrove degradation monitoring, ecological restoration assessment, and biodiversity conservation.

title: Wavelet-guided decomposition of two-dimensional InSAR time series: insights into long-term settlement and cyclic deformation of a high earth-rockfill dam
abstract: Long-term deformation of high earth-rockfill dams reflects post-construction consolidation, creep, reservoir loading, and cyclic operation. Separating these superimposed components is essential for gaining process-level insights into spatial patterns and differential responses. This study investigates the Pubugou Dam, a 186 m high earth-rockfill dam in Southwest China, using ascending and descending Sentinel-1 observations from 2017–2023. The two viewing geometries were jointly inverted to recover vertical and east-west displacements. A wavelet-guided decomposition, in which dominant periods identified by the continuous wavelet transform constrain the window length and component grouping in singular spectrum analysis, was proposed to separate the displacement records into long-term trend, annual cyclic, and residual components. Synthetic experiments yielded root mean square errors of 0.69–2.16 mm, indicating effective decomposition performance. Cross wavelet transform and wavelet transform coherence quantified localized coherence and phase lags between the cyclic components and reservoir water level. The central earth-rockfill body exhibits the largest magnitudes of vertical and east-west deformation rates, whereas the spillway and abutments remained comparatively stable. The trend components and settlement indices are consistent with relatively slow long-term post-construction settlement during the observation period. Annual cyclic deformation is more pronounced in the east-west direction and exhibits spatially variable lags relative to reservoir level fluctuations. Settlement inclination and apparent horizontal strain remain low under the adopted criteria, suggesting limited crest-cracking susceptibility during the observation period. This work demonstrates how wavelet-guided decomposition of two-dimensional InSAR time series provides spatially explicit insights into long-term settlement and cyclic deformation of high earth-rockfill dams.

title: Learning Complex Scene Segmentation from Noisy Label
SkinTokens : A Learned Compact Representation for Unified Autoregressive Rigging
abstract: The rapid proliferation of generative 3D models has created a critical bottleneck in animation pipelines: rigging. Existing automated methods are fundamentally limited by their approach to skinning, treating it as an ill-posed, high-dimensional regression task that is inefficient to optimize and is typically decoupled from skeleton generation. We posit this is a representation problem and introduce SkinTokens : a learned, compact, and discrete representation for skinning weights. By leveraging an FSQ-CVAE to capture the intrinsic sparsity of skinning, we reframe the task from continuous regression to a more tractable token sequence prediction problem. This representation enables TokenRig , a unified autoregressive framework that models the entire rig as a single sequence of skeletal parameters and SkinTokens, learning the complicated dependencies between skeletons and skin deformations. The unified model is then amenable to a reinforcement learning stage, where tailored geometric and semantic rewards improve generalization to complex, out-of-distribution assets. Quantitatively, the SkinTokens representation leads to a 98%–133% relative improvement in skinning-weight L 1 error over state-of-the-art methods, while the full TokenRig framework, refined with RL, improves the skeletal Chamfer distance by 17%–22% . Our work presents a unified, generative approach to rigging that yields higher fidelity and robustness, offering a scalable solution to a long-standing challenge in 3D content creation.

title: Dust aerosol properties and radiative effects over the global oceans from synergistic spaceborne observations and modeling
Development and validation of a red-edge-based index for improving satellite detection of algal blooms in inland waters
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: The increasing frequency of freshwater algal blooms threatens aquatic ecosystems globally. While remote sensing algorithms are widely used for bloom detection, conventional methods frequently exhibit degraded performance under optically complex conditions (e.g., sunglint, thin clouds, and high turbidity) and lack sensitivity to sparse blooms. To address these limitations, this study introduces the Red-Edge Floating Algae Index (RFAI). Structured as a baseline-height model, the RFAI mathematically isolates the scattering-induced spectral curvature of algal blooms using three critical Sentinel-2 Multispectral Instrument (MSI) bands: the green reflectance peak (∼560 nm), the red absorption trough (∼665 nm), and the red-edge reflectance peak (∼704 nm). This formulation effectively decouples genuine target signals from confounding background noise. Comparative validation against 17 widely used indices across a diverse set of inland lakes demonstrated the statistically significant overall effectiveness of the RFAI ( p < 0.0001), yielding precision and F1-score improvements of up to 42.8 % and 26.6 %, respectively, under locally optimized parameterizations. Crucially, the RFAI demonstrates robust comprehensive stability across highly variable, optically challenging conditions, effectively mitigating the severe performance fluctuations often observed in individual conventional indices. Supported by a novel optical-type-stratified thresholding strategy, the RFAI establishes a scalable and versatile framework for operational bloom monitoring using compatible red-edge satellite systems, enabling the generation of reliable observational records essential for the sustainable management of aquatic ecosystems.

title: Reconstructing multi-temporal Glacier area changes to improve mass balance estimates in the Southeastern Tibetan Plateau (2000–2025)
abstract: The southeastern Tibetan Plateau (SETP), a critical component of the “Asian Water Tower”, hosts a large concentration of maritime temperate glaciers that are highly sensitive to climate change. However, persistent cloud cover, seasonal snow, and supraglacial debris complicate consistent long-term glacier mapping, while the use of static glacier boundaries may introduce temporal mismatches in altimetry-based glacier mass-change estimates. In this study, we developed a multi-source data-fusion framework on Google Earth Engine (GEE) to reconstruct glacier-area changes in the SETP from 2000 to 2025 at five-year intervals and 30 m spatial resolution. Random Forest classifiers were used to integrate Landsat and Sentinel-2 optical imagery, Sentinel-1 synthetic-aperture-radar data, and NASADEM-derived topographic information, supporting glacier delineation under complex surface and atmospheric conditions. The reconstructed glacier area decreased from 8,083 ± 664 km2 in 2000 to 6,228 ± 572 km2 in 2025, corresponding to a cumulative loss of 22.9 ± 3.6% and a mean loss rate of 80.51 ± 10.51 km2 yr−1. The mean area-loss rates were 51.31 ± 6.51 km2 yr−1 during 2000–2010 and 92.99 ± 15.55 km2 yr−1 during 2010–2025, indicating a higher average loss rate in the later period. By combining satellite-altimetry-derived elevation changes from ICESat, CryoSat-2, and ICESat-2 with the reconstructed time-varying glacier areas, we estimated a mean glacier mass-change rate of −6.51 ± 1.22 Gt yr−1 during 2003–2022. Compared with using a fixed 2003 glacier area, the time-varying-area calculation reduced the estimated mass-loss magnitude by 0.63 Gt yr−1, equivalent to 8.8% of the fixed-area estimate. These results indicate that incorporating time-varying glacier areas can reduce temporal mismatch in altimetry-based mass-change estimation and improve the temporal consistency of regional glacier mass-change assessments.

title: A Metro-InSAR Risk Index for corridor-scale displacement risk diagnosis of urban rail infrastructure
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Time-series Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) provides dense displacement observations along urban rail corridors, yet converting point-based measurements into corridor-scale diagnostic information remains challenging. This study proposes the Metro-InSAR Risk Index (MIRI), a diagnostic index designed to convert multi-dimensional InSAR-derived displacement characteristics into displacement-related diagnostic levels for urban metro corridors. MIRI integrates displacement rate, cumulative displacement, local displacement heterogeneity, height-related variability, and temporal residual variability, thereby extending conventional velocity-based interpretation toward corridor-scale displacement-risk diagnosis. The framework was applied to the Kunming Metro Network using 198 descending Sentinel-1 images acquired from March 2018 to December 2024. The time-series InSAR results show that the network was generally stable, with line-of-sight (LOS) displacement rates mainly ranging from −6 to 3 mm/yr and 97.21% of coherent scatterers falling within the stable interval of −3 to 3 mm/yr. Localized displacement anomalies were mainly observed near line intersections, curved sections, construction-affected areas, and the Dianchi Lake shoreline. Based on MIRI, 78%, 17%, 4%, and 1% of valid points were classified as Levels D, C, B, and A, respectively, indicating a distribution dominated by lower diagnostic levels, with spatially confined Level-B and Level-A anomalies particularly along Lines 4 and 5 and in lakeside soft-ground areas. Multi-source contextual variables and XGBoost-SHAP analysis were further used to interpret the environmental, anthropogenic, operational, and displacement-gradient information associated with the MIRI-based diagnostic patterns. The results indicate that the spatial variation in MIRI is mainly associated with terrain-related conditions, corridor-scale displacement variation, metro operation, and urban development intensity. By deriving diagnostic levels directly from PSI-based displacement indicators, MIRI provides an InSAR-based screening tool for prioritizing displacement-related anomalies and supporting maintenance of urban rail transit systems.

title: Second-dimension-enhanced spatial context-aware modeling for spatial prediction
abstract: Spatial prediction is a fundamental task in geographic information science and environmental resource assessment. However, under complex terrain and heterogeneous covariates, models relying only on point-scale attributes or a single global relationship often have difficulty representing spatial context and regional heterogeneity. This study proposes a second-dimension-enhanced spatial context-aware modeling framework (SDA-SCA) that integrates first-dimension covariates, neighborhood-based second-dimension features, covariate screening, spatially constrained stratification, and local model training. Using two independently constructed annual spatial-prediction cases based on surface solar radiation observations from 670 stations in China in 2022 and 2023, five modeling schemes—Ordinary Kriging, Geographically Weighted Random Forest (GWRF), first-dimension attribute modeling (FDA), second-dimension augmented modeling (SDA), and SDA-SCA—were evaluated under spatial cross-validation. SDA-SCA showed a consistent predictive advantage across the two independent annual cases and the three evaluated model families. Relative to FDA, SDA-SCA increased R2 by 0.11–0.16 in 2022 and 0.17–0.21 in 2023, while reducing RMSE by 12.4%–17.7% and 24.3%–33.7%, and MAE by 22.8%–35.5% and 31.5%–50.4%, respectively. Stage-wise ablation showed that the FDA-to-SDA step produced consistent but moderate improvements, whereas the SDA-to-SDA-SCA step provided larger and more stable gains. These results indicate that second-dimension features improve the representation of neighborhood context, and their predictive value is further strengthened when coupled with spatial stratification. SHAP analysis further confirmed the substantial contribution of second-dimension features to the integrated model. The proposed framework provides an extensible pathway for spatial prediction tasks requiring the joint representation of local attributes, neighborhood context, and spatial heterogeneity.

title: Prior-Informed Spatially Adaptive Network (PISA-Net) for multi-parameter water quality retrieval in Poyang Lake using Sentinel-2 imagery
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Accurate retrieval of water-quality parameters from remote-sensing imagery is essential for monitoring large inland lakes, yet pronounced spatial heterogeneity and limited transferability across varying environmental conditions remain major challenges. This study proposes a Prior-Informed Spatially Adaptive Network (PISA-Net) for multi-parameter water-quality retrieval from Sentinel-2 imagery in Poyang Lake. PISA-Net integrates a CNN branch for nonlinear spectral–spatial feature learning with a knowledge-guided branch based on empirical optical descriptors and coordinate-derived geographic priors. A geographic soft-assignment mechanism constructs the spatial prior vector, which conditions CNN features through Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FiLM), while a stop gradient consistency loss (SG-CL) promotes agreement between the two prediction pathways with controlled gradient propagation. Chl-a, TP, and CODMn were modeled independently and evaluated using 5-fold spatial-block cross-validation against six representative empirical, statistical, machine-learning, and deep-learning baselines. PISA-Net achieved R 2 values of 0.6113, 0.5112, and 0.5054 for Chl-a, TP, and CODMn, respectively, consistently outperforming the strongest baseline, 2D-CNN, while reducing RMSE by approximately 29.6%, 21.4%, and 19.0%. An additional April 2018 cross-season experiment revealed substantial degradation under direct zero-shot transfer, whereas few-shot adaptation markedly reduced prediction errors, indicating useful cross-season adaptability after limited local calibration. Overall, PISA-Net provides a prior-informed spectral–spatial framework for water-quality retrieval under spatially heterogeneous conditions, while broader multi-season validation remains necessary to establish comprehensive seasonal generalizability.

title: Developing broadband spectral index for estimating crop canopy water content
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Crop canopy water content (CWC) is an important indicator for monitoring crop growth and drought stress. However, broadband spectral indices often exhibit nonlinear and saturated responses to CWC because NIR structural scattering and SWIR water-absorption responses progressively approach saturation as leaf area index (LAI) and equivalent water thickness (EWT) increase. Because CWC is jointly determined by LAI and EWT, this study developed a physically based broadband spectral index, the Differential Ratio Water Index (DRWI), using Sentinel-2 multispectral instrument bands to couple canopy structural information from the near-infrared and red-edge regions with water-sensitive shortwave-infrared responses. PROSAIL-based global sensitivity analysis showed that DRWI had substantial and relatively balanced sensitivity to both LAI and EWT. On the independent simulated holdout dataset, DRWI showed a strong association with CWC (R 2 = 0.85) and reduced response compression compared with conventional indices. Independent validation using field-measured corn data showed that DRWI generally achieved the best numerical performance among the evaluated indices, although its advantage varied among growth stages. On the multi-crop SPARC03 dataset, DRWI achieved an R 2 of 0.58 and an rRMSE of 33.64 %, compared with an R 2 of 0.54 for LSWI. DRWI provides a physically interpretable and computationally simple approach for regional CWC estimation using widely available Sentinel-2 observations. Its predictive performance remained limited at the corn heading stage, and further evaluation across additional crop types, regions, and complete growth cycles is needed.

title: Transforming Leaf-Off LiDAR to leaf-on canopy height models using deep learning
abstract: Accurate tree canopy metrics are essential for a wide range of ecological, environmental, and climate studies. Recent advances in airborne LiDAR sensing have greatly expanded access to high-resolution three-dimensional observations of tree canopy structure. However, many widely available airborne LiDAR datasets are acquired under leaf-off conditions to support terrain mapping, and our analysis across ecologically diverse sites shows that canopy height models (CHMs) derived from these data exhibit substantial, recurring discrepancies in canopy height and extent, with an overall tendency to underrepresent canopy structure relative to leaf-on conditions. These discrepancies limit the direct use of leaf-off CHMs in applications requiring canopy information representative of leaf-on conditions. To address this limitation, we introduce a deep learning framework for reconstructing leaf-on CHMs from existing leaf-off LiDAR-derived CHMs. To our knowledge, this is the first study to formulate the direct reconstruction of leaf-on CHMs from existing leaf-off LiDAR-derived CHMs as a supervised image-to-image learning task. The framework provides two complementary models: a Pix2Pix model that uses the leaf-off CHM alone and a U-Net model that additionally incorporates multispectral imagery. Our proposed models achieve robust canopy-height accuracy across four spatially independent test sites (R²: 0.85–0.92; Mean Absolute Error: 1.3–1.6 metres), substantially reducing the discrepancies observed in the leaf-off source CHMs. They also provide sharper delineation of canopy details and higher accuracy than recent optical-imagery-based approaches. To facilitate broader use, we developed an open-access web application that deploys the pre-trained models and supports on-demand leaf-on CHM generation for user-selected areas across the U.S. where suitable leaf-off LiDAR inputs are available. Overall, the framework provides a practical means to bridge the seasonal data gap in LiDAR acquisition and improve access to reliable canopy metrics representative of leaf-on conditions.

title: Passive microwave sea ice concentration biases in the Southern Hemisphere revealed by ICESat-2 linear ice fraction
A revised model for atmospheric adjacency effect correction in optical satellite earth observation images
abstract: Adjacency effects, caused by atmospheric scattering, constitute a significant source of error in optical satellite surface reflectance retrievals, accounting for up to 50% of the measured signal near sharp reflectance contrasts. This study derives an improved analytical model for the atmospheric Point Spread Function (PSF) as a function of atmospheric and geometric parameters, using the GPU-accelerated SMART-G Monte Carlo model. Among four formulations compared, the two-parameter King kernel is the most suitable for lookup-table parameterisation across aerosol optical thickness (AOT), wavelength, aerosol species and vertical distribution, relative humidity, viewing geometry, and ground elevation. For artificial landscapes, the King model reduces the RMSE of surface reflectance retrieval by a factor of 3 to 11 compared to Wu et al., 2024, and by more than one order of magnitude compared to the widely used Gaussian model, at nadir and off-nadir angles up to 16 ∘ . Validation on Sentinel-2 scenes over Cairo and Arcachon Bay confirms relative TOA errors below 1% for the King model, while the Gaussian model systematically underestimates reflectance in high-contrast areas. Comparison with in-situ marine reflectances from the GLORIA dataset shows RMSE reductions of up to 57% over the Gaussian model and up to 11% over Wu et al., 2024 in the near-infrared. A sensitivity analysis shows that AOT is the dominant parameter, followed by wavelength, aerosol species and vertical distribution, while solar zenith angle has no influence for Lambertian surfaces and viewing zenith angle is negligible within the Sentinel-2 field of view.

title: UrbanQGS: Large-scale urban surface reconstruction via analytic curvature consistency in quadratic Gaussian splatting
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
abstract: Large-scale 3D surface reconstruction at the city scale from UAV imagery is a core task for building digital-twin cities. Although 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) and its variants have achieved remarkable progress in radiance-field reconstruction, existing methods still struggle with scale-varying structural complexity and diverse urban textures: geometry is often incomplete in low-frequency, weak-texture regions over large areas, while in high-frequency regions with intricate details, disordered primitive distributions tend to cause floating artifacts and outliers. To address these issues, we propose UrbanQGS, a large-scale urban reconstruction framework built on quadratic Gaussian splatting. We inherit quadratic surface Gaussians as scene primitives and use their analytic curvature as the central driving signal to perform a two-stage geometric refinement: (1) A self-supervised geometric constraint based on cross-view curvature consistency, which effectively fills geometric holes in weak-texture planar regions. (2) A curvature-aware adaptive representation allocation strategy that reweights, recalibrates, and ranks densification gradients, guiding split and clone operations toward geometrically complex regions while standard pruning removes redundant primitives. In addition, we integrate a monocular normal prior to correct global orientation drift during large-scale reconstruction. We further assess the compatibility of UrbanQGS with partitioned large-scene reconstruction using a visibility-aware block-wise protocol with hardware-constrained per-block budgets. The blocks are trained sequentially on a single GPU. Experiments on large-scale UAV datasets demonstrate that, compared with state-of-the-art 3DGS-based large-scale reconstruction methods, UrbanQGS maintains superior geometric quality while substantially reducing redundant Gaussians and mesh complexity, yielding finer and more complete geometric structures, while qualitative results on our custom-collected dataset indicate its compatibility with a partitioned large-scene reconstruction pipeline.

title: Assessing the spatio-temporal cumulative drought effects on two Mediterranean forest types in Central Chile
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Droughts are long-lasting events that can drive persistent functional changes in ecosystems, particularly in drought-prone areas like Mediterranean forests. We integrated a phenology-based anomaly method, combining kernel density estimation (KDE) with cumulative sums (CUSUMs) to assess long-term drought impacts on two Mediterranean forest types in Central Chile. Using MODIS Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI), the Moisture Stress Index (MSI), and Evapotranspiration (ET) from 2000 to 2024, we quantified cumulative deviations in canopy productivity, moisture conditions, and energy exchange. Our framework revealed persistent negative functional trajectories preceding the well-documented 2010–present megadrought. Spatially explicit metrics identified coherent degradation hotspots in northern sclerophyllous and southern deciduous forests, where canopy greenness, moisture, and evapotranspiration declined synchronously. Seasonal models indicated a post-2010 strengthening of soil–water controls over forest functioning, with soil moisture and water storage variables becoming influential predictors. The convergence of cumulative negative EVI, MSI, and ET signals highlights widespread and sustained functional weakening under prolonged drought conditions. Our results demonstrate that integrating KDE-derived anomalies with cumulative deviation tracking provides a sensitive and transferable framework to detect early and persistent vegetation stress in water-limited ecosystems.

title: Deep learning detection of submesoscale eddies from MODIS SST in the South China Sea
abstract: Submesoscale eddies play crucial roles in oceanic energy cascades and material transport; however, their detection faces substantial challenges owing to inadequate spatial resolution in traditional satellite altimetric measurements. This research introduces Sub-Eddy-Net, an innovative deep learning approach utilizing an enhanced YOLOv8-SGAM architecture for identifying submesoscale eddy features within MODIS-derived sea surface temperature (SST) imagery across the South China Sea region. By exploiting SST data's advantageous temporal coverage and observational continuity relative to altimetric sensors, synthetic aperture radar, and ocean color products, the developed algorithm demonstrates detection precision of 0.968, successfully identifying 20,443 submesoscale eddies throughout 2015–2024. Results indicate cyclonic eddy prevalence exceeds anticyclonic occurrences, exhibiting average radii of 13.1 km and 13.7 km respectively. Eddy distributions primarily cluster within coastal waters and Luzon Strait vicinity, displaying pronounced seasonal patterns. Comparison with Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) observations shows 64.3% matched features, 27.1% positional offsets, and 8.6% detected only in SST. Within the same eddies, coherent chlorophyll-a (Chla) signatures were present in a smaller fraction, indicating that SST is the more robust tracer for systematic detection. This Sub-Eddy-Net methodology offers a scalable approach for examining submesoscale oceanic phenomena, providing a decadal inventory for further study of their roles in ocean circulation and vertical exchange.

title: Integrating Landsat and ECOSTRESS to explore the value of additional thermal infrared satellite observations for field-scale evapotranspiration mapping
abstract: Landsat has provided an indispensable foundation for field-scale evapotranspiration (ET) mapping but is constrained by its overpass temporal frequency. Although integrating additional thermal data offers a pathway to bridge this gap, the magnitude of improvement varies across observation characteristics and surface context and remains less understood. Here, ECOsystem Spaceborne Thermal Radiometer Experiment on Space Station (ECOSTRESS) is used as an additional thermal source on top of the Landsat baseline to evaluate the value of more frequent thermal observations for improving field-scale ET time series. We implemented a Google Earth Engine -based Disaggregated Atmosphere-Land Exchange Inverse + Data Mining Sharpener framework to generate a Landsat-based ET baseline and enhanced it with ECOSTRESS observations. The resulting ET data was validated across 25 flux-tower sites spanning diverse land-cover types and climate zones across the contiguous United States. When integrated with Landsat, the addition of ECOSTRESS observations reduced interpolation errors and improved temporal consistency across most sites. However, improvements in ET time series agreement depended strongly on (1) the extent to which ECOSTRESS reduced effective Landsat sampling gaps and (2) the accuracy of overpass-day ECOSTRESS ET retrievals. Improvements were largest when ECOSTRESS shortened Landsat observation gaps by ~50% and maintained high scene quality. ECOSTRESS overpass time also influenced performance, with acquisitions between 10:00–14:00 producing most reliable ET estimates. These results support developing methods with multi-satellite observations to strengthen field-scale ET and help address the key knowledge gap regarding the value of increased thermal observations.

title: Twin-satellite constraints from GF-5B and DQ-1 enable hourly near-surface NO2 estimation across China
abstract: Nitrogen dioxide (NO 2 ) is a major air pollutant with significant impacts on human health, yet satellite-based estimates of surface NO 2 with full diurnal coverage remain limited. Here, we develop a machine learning framework to estimate hourly near-surface NO 2 concentrations across China by integrating complementary observations from two Chinese polar-orbiting satellites, GF-5B (~10:30 local time) and DQ-1 (~13:30 local time). A Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) model driven by twin-satellite NO 2 vertical column densities (VCDs) and meteorological reanalysis achieves strong predictive performance in 10-fold cross-validation, with a coefficient of determination (R 2 ) of 0.91 and root mean square error (RMSE) of 5.40 μg/m 3 across all hours (4.46 μg/m 3 during daytime; 6.32 μg/m 3 at night), and retains reasonable skill under stricter site-based, time-based, and independent cross-year validation. The reconstructed dataset captures the characteristic diurnal cycle of NO 2 , with morning and evening peaks associated with traffic emissions and a midday minimum driven by photochemical loss. Compared to the single-satellite TROPOMI product, the twin-satellite configuration substantially improves the representation of diurnal variability, increasing R 2 from 0.81 to 0.91 and reducing RMSE by 31.60%, and corrects a distorted urban-rural NO 2 exposure ratio (1.70 for TROPOMI versus a ground-based 1.19), narrowing it to 1.30. Feature-importance analysis further shows that meteorological variables dominate model predictions during both day and night, with satellite VCDs providing a complementary, though indirect, constraint on nighttime concentrations. The resulting hourly NO 2 dataset demonstrates the value of synergistic multi-satellite observations for air quality monitoring and provides a robust basis for refined pollution control and population exposure assessment.

title: Advanced characterization of the diurnal variations of aerosol optical and microphysical properties by SYREMIS/GRASP synergistic retrieval algorithm using observations from multiple spaceborne sensors
abstract: Accurate characterization of the diurnal variation of aerosol optical and microphysical properties—including Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD), Angstrom Exponent (AE), and Single Scattering Albedo (SSA)—is fundamental for climate and air quality modeling. However, retrieving high-temporal-resolution, physically consistent aerosol products from multiple satellite instruments remains a challenge. Current multi-satellite approaches often rely on “post-retrieval” merging of independent Level-2 products, a process that frequently introduces physical inconsistencies and artificial temporal oscillations. To address this, building upon the recently established SYREMIS/GRASP synergetic retrieval framework (Litvinov et al., 2025), an inversion approach based on harmonized Level-1 satellite measurements, this study extensively evaluates its performance in capturing aerosol diurnal variability. We evaluate two configurations: (i) LEO + LEO synergy (Sentinel-3 A/B OLCI and Sentinel-5P TROPOMI) and (ii) LEO + GEO synergy (integrating Himawari-8 AHI). By enforcing multi-pixel smoothness constraints within the retrieval, SYREMIS maintains high physical consistency across instruments, effectively mitigating the structural discrepancies and “noise” inherent in standard merging techniques. Our validation against AERONET ground-based data and intercomparison with the XAERDT product suite confirm that SYREMIS provides high retrieval stability and accuracy. Without applying post-retrieval quality filtering, SYREMIS achieves an AOD GCOS fulfillment percentage of up to 70%, an AE RMSE below 0.3, and an SSA “Optimal” requirement fulfillment rate of up to 85% at representative sites. We demonstrate the framework's capability to resolve rapid aerosol dynamics through case studies of biomass-burning events over Thailand and Myanmar, as well as dust pollution over Qatar in 2019. As a three-month proof-of-concept assessment (March–May 2019) , these results highlight the practical capability of the established SYREMIS/GRASP approach to generate high-resolution, physically consistent, and stable aerosol data records from the measurements of multiple satellites.

title: Constructive solid geometry for automatic topology-aware BIM reconstruction from point clouds
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
abstract: The automatic reconstruction of Building Information Models (BIMs) remains challenging, especially when applied to multi-storey buildings and indoor environments with non-Manhattan layouts and curved structures. To address these challenges, this paper presents a novel method that places Constructive Solid Geometry (CSG) at the core of building reconstruction from point clouds. The methodology also integrates the Segment Anything Model (SAM) and knowledge-based rules to reconstruct as-built BIMs while preserving the geometry and topology of building elements. The proposed approach consists of two main stages: SAM-based segmentation and CSG-based modelling. First, SAM is used to segment rooms, as well as door and window openings. Solids are then generated for the indoor spaces and openings. Finally, a set of Boolean operations is applied to reconstruct building elements, including slabs, walls, indoor spaces, doors, and windows, while subtracting openings of doors, windows, and staircases. Finally, the reconstructed model is encoded with semantic information following the Industry Foundation Classes (IFC) schema. The method was evaluated on seven two-storey building point clouds and demonstrated strong performance, achieving a mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) greater than 90% for floor plan reconstruction, a precision above 87% for door and window detection, and mean geometric deviations below 8 cm for BIM reconstruction.

title: SkySplat++: Hierarchical 3D Gaussian Splatting for generalizable sparse-view reconstruction from multi-temporal satellite imagery
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing

title: A GeoAI framework for remote-sensing-driven traffic activity and emission intensity in a data-scarce megacity
abstract: In rapidly expanding megacities across the Global South, a profound data scarcity paradox frequently prevents effective environmental monitoring and evidence driven urban planning. While severe traffic congestion generates acute localised pollution, the total absence of continuous municipal traffic counters, ubiquitous vehicle telemetry, and air quality monitoring networks leaves these environments empirically unmonitored. This study resolves this challenge by introducing a reproducible geocomputational framework designed to map microscale traffic activity and relative emission landscapes by fusing multisource geospatial data and deep learning workflows. Focusing on the unmonitored context of Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo, our methodology uses very high resolution 15 cm satellite imagery to train and deploy a localised YOLOv8 (You Only Look Once, version 8) computer vision model, establishing an empirical baseline of fleet distribution. These static counts are dynamically distributed across the urban road network using a probabilistic Hub and Spoke Gravity Model, which is weighted through a zero shot Large Language Model semantic reclassification of unstructured OpenStreetMap features. Reconstructed kinematic flows are subsequently processed through velocity dependent Tier 3 EMEP/EEA algorithms to capture the nonlinear emission penalties triggered by severe network gridlock. To ensure framework defensibility, an independent unmanned aerial vehicle observation campaign was executed across ten distinct urban sites. The drone data directly validate model estimated physical parameters, achieving robust correlations for traffic volumes (R2 = 0.826) and link speeds (R2 = 0.925). Because literature derived chemical emission factors cannot be validated in situ, all absolute outputs are subjected to a rigorous multiparameter sensitivity analysis to report findings strictly as bounded ranges. The results reveal a clear structural handover in the spatial activity profile of the city. Daytime pollution is heavily driven by the informal paratransit fleet, which accounts for a bounded range of 82.8% to 95.1% of total PM2.5 emissions along primary corridors despite representing a numerical minority of active vehicles. Conversely, nocturnal baseline emissions transition to a landscape dominated almost entirely by private passenger vehicles. All code, processing pipelines, and validation datasets are available in a FAIR compliant open access repository. This framework establishes a scalable, remote sensing driven blueprint for diagnosing traffic activity structures in unmonitored metropolitan regions worldwide.

title: Substantial disagreement between satellite- and ground-level nighttime light patterns revealed by SDGSAT-1 and street view imagery
abstract: Over the past three decades, nighttime light (NTL) has become one of the most widely used and powerful proxies for characterizing human activities. Despite the recent proliferation of available NTL data from both satellite- and ground-level sensors, intrinsic differences between these two observation approaches can result in distinct NTL brightness patterns (satellite-ground disagreement). Such disagreement, particularly its spatial heterogeneity, represents a critical yet largely overlooked issue in NTL studies, introducing uncertainty into the interpretation and application of NTL observations. Here, by incorporating SDGSAT-1 glimmer imagery and panoramic nighttime street view imagery with geospatial AI approaches, we present a spatially explicit, wall-to-wall investigation into satellite-ground disagreement across Singapore. Specifically, we characterized citywide disagreement and its variation across land-use types, analyzed contributing factors, and assessed its implications for NTL-based applications, reinforced by Monte Carlo-based uncertainty quantification and sensitivity analyses using independent observations from Singapore and Shenzhen, China. Our study revealed substantial and spatially heterogeneous satellite-ground disagreement across Singapore. Relative disagreement averaged 15% ± 13% citywide but reached 42% ± 12% in 13% of the city. Such pronounced heterogeneity was likewise evident across land-use types, with commercial areas standing out for consistently significant disagreement, where ground-level NTL brightness was 29% ± 26% higher than satellite-level NTL brightness. Building morphology, vegetation canopy cover, and sensor spectral response contributed to satellite-ground disagreement, suggestive of distinct mechanisms underlying the identified patterns. Applying satellite- and ground-level NTL data yielded relative differences of at least 115% and 83% in GDP estimation and NTL exposure inequality assessment, respectively. This study sheds new light on satellite-ground disagreement by moving beyond discrete comparisons toward a comprehensive analysis of its heterogeneity and implications, thereby establishing an empirical basis for integrating NTL observations and contributing to more reliable NTL-based applications and evidence-informed policies on sustainable urbanization.

title: Evaluating multi-satellite VIIRS active fire observations as a burned area proxy across North America
abstract: Wildfire activity fundamentally regulates terrestrial carbon dynamics and atmospheric emissions, necessitating timely and spatially complete mapping of burned area. Traditional reflectance-based burned area products provide robust spatial records but often have multi-week to multi-month processing latencies that limit near-real-time applications. Active-fire detections provide low-latency observations, but their use as a burned area proxy is constrained by temporal sampling gaps and commission errors associated with sub-pixel fire detection. This study represents one of the first applications to use the full three-satellite Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS) constellation, comprising S-NPP, NOAA-20, and NOAA-21, to address these limitations. Here, we evaluate how the spatial performance of a cumulative VIIRS active-fire approach varies with temporal sampling, latitude, and fire regime. We developed a VIIRS Cumulative Active Fire (VCAF) approach using the 375-m VIIRS active-fire record across North America from 2012 to 2024, and evaluated its spatial agreement with visually interpreted reference labels and the North American Fire History (NAFH) dataset, using MCD64A1 as a benchmark burned area product. Results from the first full year of the three-satellite configuration (2024) indicate that VCAF had higher spatial agreement than MCD64A1 in parts of the high-latitude domain (>50°N), with particularly high patch-level recall for small reference burned patches (<100 ha) while maintaining high recall for large patches (>1000 ha). The observed performance varied substantially with latitude and fire regime. In high-latitude boreal regions, the greater potential sampling frequency of the VIIRS constellation was associated with lower omission errors and greater spatial completeness in some regions, although environmental conditions such as persistent cloud cover remained important limitations. In contrast, VCAF systematically overestimated burned area in fragmented lower-latitude fire regimes. These results indicate that multi-satellite VIIRS active-fire observations can provide a potentially useful burned area proxy in selected high-latitude fire regimes and highlight the importance of accounting for temporal sampling and fire-regime characteristics when interpreting active-fire-based burned area estimates.

title: Divergent transpiration regulation among 20 urban tree species under extreme heat revealed by UAV multisource remote sensing
DynamicVis: Dynamic visual perception for efficient remote sensing foundation models
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing

title: Global cross-modal geo-localization: A million-scale dataset and a physical consistency learning framework
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing

title: Breaking modal barriers: Achieving modality-balanced semantic segmentation across optical and SAR images through optical image-supervised learning
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: As the two primary imaging modalities in remote sensing, optics and Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) have been widely applied in semantic segmentation tasks. However, the scarcity of annotated samples in SAR images limits the performance of related models. How to leverage the abundant annotated samples of optical images to achieve modality-balanced semantic segmentation capabilities across both optical and SAR modalities is of great significance for all-weather interpretation. Restricted by the complexity of modality perception, achieving balanced cross-modal segmentation still faces significant challenges. To address the above issues, we fully consider the modal balance and reliability of knowledge transfer in modal migration and propose a modality-balanced knowledge distillation (MBKD) transfer learning framework. By generating and learning virtual modalities and stitched modalities, a cross-modal migration task is transformed into two symmetric intra-modal migration subtasks, explicitly promoting balanced knowledge transfer between modalities. To demonstrate the effectiveness and practicality of the proposed framework, we conducted application experiments on the large-scale public dataset WHU-OPT-SAR, MULTISENGE-6, and in 6 provinces of China. The results show that our method significantly outperforms other approaches in terms of both performance and stability.

title: GeoSeg-SAM: Task-aligned adaptation of SAM for geological remote sensing interpretation
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: The Segment Anything Model (SAM) has shown strong performance in natural image segmentation. However, its direct transfer to geological environment remote sensing (GERS) is limited by significant domain discrepancies. GERS elements typically exhibit high class diversity, strong inter-class similarity, and imbalanced sample distribution, which challenge SAM’s prompt-driven paradigm in maintaining semantic stability and spatial contextual consistency. To bridge this gap, we propose GeoSeg-SAM, a geological task-aligned adaptation framework built upon SAM. GeoSeg-SAM progressively aligns generic visual features with geology-discriminative semantics through layer-wise semantic adapters, and introduces a dual-scale structure-aware module in the deeper encoder layers to enhance global region-level contextual representation. Meanwhile, the model employs Pyramid Residual Aggregation (PRA) to fuse multi-level geological semantic representations across stages, thereby improving the representational capacity of features. In addition, at the mask prediction stage, decoded features are fused with PRA-based semantic representations using a semantics-constrained fusion decoding strategy, and a single geological semantic token is incorporated to enhance semantic consistency in GERS scenarios. Experimental results on three representative GERS study areas show that GeoSeg-SAM improves mIoU by approximately 3 percentage points or more over the best competing method in each area, confirming its effectiveness in GERS image interpretation tasks. Code is available at: https://github.com/WanZhan-lucky/GeoSeg-SAM .

title: MCHex: marching cubes based adaptive hexahedral mesh generation with guaranteed positive Jacobian
abstract: Grid-based methods are robust for automatic hexahedral (hex) meshing, but struggle with boundary fidelity and element quality. Conventional pipelines remove outside elements, yielding axis-aligned surfaces converging to the input geometry at first order; subsequent padding and projection are heuristic, offering no guarantees on final boundary fidelity or mesh quality. This paper introduces MCHex, a fundamental reformulation of boundary and mesh-quality handling in grid-based hex meshing. MCHex applies marching cubes (MC) inside each grid cell, ensuring the mesh boundary is an MC surface. The key insight is that constraining cut-cell configurations to 3-regular polyhedra and applying midpoint subdivision produces an all-hex mesh with guaranteed positive Jacobian for every element. MCHex provides three advantages: (1) theoretical positive-Jacobian guarantee for every element; (2) boundary convergence matching MC’s approximation rate, via a non-heuristic algorithm with well-bounded time complexity and the fastest wall-clock time among existing methods; and (3) manifold surfaces for arbitrary geometries plus a natural padded layer. Extensive evaluation on 202 benchmark geometries, using a slightly smaller element budget, compares MCHex with previous state-of-the-art methods; it consistently yields positive-Jacobian meshes with similar boundary fidelity while running significantly faster. It integrates seamlessly with post-processing such as smoothing and simplification, and is suitable for simulation.

title: A decade of summer glacier fronts and calved glacier ice distribution in Kongs- and Krossfjorden, Svalbard, observed by Sentinel-1 extra wide swath
abstract: A statistical method to map atmospheric exposure is applied on the whole decade (2015–2024) of Sentinel-1 summer acquisitions in Extra Wide Swath mode over Kongs- and Krossfjorden on Svalbard. The consistent daily observations not only allow to statistically define a summer glacier front extent of marine-terminating glaciers but also reveal a new application, which is to detect the summer distribution of calved glacier ice, i.e. icebergs, bergy bits and growlers (IBG). These originate from glacier calving during the sea-ice free period. Summer glacier extent that we define statistically as the area where the glacier prevails more than 95% during summer co-locate well with independent glacier fronts digitized from Sentinel-2 optical imagery. Annual summer IBG distributions are classified into percentage ranges of temporal occurrence, representing the proportion of time IBG are detected in the corresponding pixel location. The ten-year record of mean annual summer IBG-occupied areas is compared to separate estimates of summer glacier frontal ablation for the two glaciers Lillehöökbreen and Kronebreen. The comparison indicates a clear link between mean summer calved ice distribution area and the glaciers' frontal ablation with correlation coefficients (r) of 0.67 and 0.85 for Lillehöökbreen and Kronebreen, respectively. Frontal ablation includes both calving and submarine/subaerial melting at the glacier front and combining this with IBG occurrence estimates may provide new insights into the mass loss ratio between calving and melting. However, the relationship between IBG occurrence distribution and frontal ablation appears to be glacier specific. As this study represents a first attempt to map IBG occurrence distribution and mean IBG occupied area and link that to glacier frontal ablation, further studies and application on other glaciers and fjord systems are required to fully assess the potential and limitations of mapping such IBG distribution as a proxy for glacier calving intensities.

title: From national to global: Mapping global center-pivot irrigated cropland with knowledge-guided data augmentation
Integrating multi-source physical knowledge into deep learning for satellite soil moisture downscaling
abstract: Fine-resolution soil moisture (SM) is essential for understanding land–atmosphere interactions and managing hydrological hazards at local scales. Passive microwave remote sensing provides reliable SM observations but is limited by its coarse spatial resolution. Spatial downscaling offers an important means of addressing this limitation. However, many existing downscaling methods either rely on physical models with over-simplifications of soil hydrological knowledge, or data-driven models (particularly Deep Learning, DL) that lack interpretability, while current physics-guided DL approaches often emphasize a limited number of physical relationships or constraints. In response, this study proposes a framework to integrate multi-source physical knowledge into DL for satellite SM downscaling. Specifically, the framework incorporates physically informed drivers, a DisPATCh-informed physical regression branch, a hydrologically motivated consistency loss, and a constrained SM boundary loss, while using a gating module to adaptively fuse physically guided and data-driven representations. Evaluations based on in-situ and aircraft SM observations, together with coarse-scale consistency checks against SMAP SM, show that the proposed framework can effectively downscale SMAP SM from 9 km to 500 m. Using region-specific models across ten environmentally diverse regions, MPhy achieved station-averaged Pearson’s R and ubRMSE values of 0.76 and 0.05 m3/m3, respectively; the corresponding values for the pure-DL baseline Dens were 0.68 and 0.06 m3/m3. Detailed experiments in WGEW further showed that MPhy generally performed better than the pure-DL baseline, DisPATCh, single-physics-informed models, and selected conventional machine-learning methods. Overall, the results support improved physical plausibility and convergence efficiency, as well as framework robustness across the evaluated environments.

title: Adaptive smooth constrained stereo matching and disparity refinement for satellite DSM generation
abstract: High-resolution satellite images often exhibit substantial geometric and radiometric differences, making it difficult for conventional stereo matching methods to achieve high matching accuracy while suppressing noise and preserving object boundaries. To address this issue, this study improves both stereo matching and disparity post-processing in the satellite digital surface model (DSM) generation workflow. First, within the semi-global matching (SGM) framework, a mixed matching cost is constructed by combining the Census transform and gradient descriptors. Image gradients and edge cues extracted by a pretrained PiDiNet are then incorporated to adaptively control the strength of the smoothness constraint during cost aggregation, thereby improving matching reliability while balancing noise suppression and disparity-boundary preservation. Second, we propose a disparity post-processing method that combines improved weighted least-squares disparity refinement with matching-cost-based disparity fusion. The method first dynamically adjusts the smoothing weights to reduce texture-copying artifacts and edge blurring and then fuses disparity using matching costs to alleviate staircase artifacts caused by excessive smoothing. Experiments were conducted on ZY3-02 and WorldView-3 satellite imagery, with SGM, S2P-HD, Agisoft Metashape software, guided aggregation net, and FoundationStereo included for comparison. Across three test scenes dominated by urban and agricultural areas, the proposed method increased the proportion of pixels with absolute elevation errors below 2 m by an average of 4.12 percentage points and reduced RMSE by an average of 0.11 m compared with standard SGM. Qualitative results further show that the proposed method effectively suppresses noise in relatively flat regions while preserving building boundaries.

title: A large-scale spatiotemporal NDVI prediction method coupling multivariable constraints and structured modeling
abstract: Accurate prediction of vegetation dynamics is essential for understanding terrestrial ecosystems carbon and water cycles. However, existing Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) prediction methods are limited in their ability to represent spatiotemporal heterogeneity and nonlinear interactions among multiple driving variables, which restrict predictive accuracy and extrapolation performance at large scales. To address these limitations, this study proposed a structured large-scale NDVI spatiotemporal prediction method incorporating multivariable constraints (MCS-LSTP) to characterize vegetation dynamics in complex and heterogeneous environments. MCS-LSTP incorporates multiple key driving variables and enhances the comprehensive representation of complex spatiotemporal dependencies and spatial heterogeneity through homogeneous spatial unit partitioning, unit-level temporal modeling, and continuous surface reconstruction. Results showed that MCS-LSTP model exhibited superior performance in terms of stability and prediction accuracy when compared to AutoRegressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA), Random Forest (RF), and Transformer models. The mean Population Stability Index (PSI) reached 0.0572, with 98.7% of prediction units exhibiting PSI values below 0.1, indicating no significant deviation between the observed and simulated NDVI values. The average R2 and RMSE on the test set were 0.8551 and 0.2171, respectively. Furthermore, MCS-LSTP accurately reproduced seasonal NDVI fluctuations and meridional spatial gradients, with particularly high agreement between simulated and reference values during the growing season. This study provides a robust and scalable solution for large-scale NDVI spatiotemporal prediction and offers critical technical support for ecological risk assessment in the Yellow River Basin and other ecologically vulnerable regions.

title: Hillslope-scale daily snow cover reconstruction in complex mountains: a novel framework integrating long-term snow persistence
abstract: Spatially continuous daily snow cover mapping at the hillslope scale (<100 m) is essential for resolving terrain-induced heterogeneity in hydrological processes and supporting mountain infrastructure management. Yet accurately characterizing daily snow cover heterogeneity at this scale remains challenging due to observational limitations and the difficulty of resolving terrain-controlled snow accumulation and ablation dynamics. To address this challenge, we developed a hillslope-scale daily snow cover reconstruction (HDSR) framework that explicitly incorporates long-term snow persistence as a structural spatial prior. The framework reconciles coarse-resolution daily Normalized Difference Snow Index (NDSI) observations with a 30 m climatological snow cover frequency (SCOF) dataset, which characterizes terrain-mediated long-term snow persistence and constrains the spatial allocation of daily snow cover at the sub-pixel scale. HDSR is implemented through three sequential stages: spatiotemporal continuity restoration (STR), SCOF-constrained spatial refinement (SSR), and spatiotemporal snow-cover inference (SSI). A high-quality 30 m reference dataset was first constructed using the Snow Mapping Algorithm Considering Different Lighting Conditions (SALC), which was identified as the optimal approach through a systematic evaluation of seven candidate snow-mapping methods. The HDSR framework was subsequently applied to the Qilian Mountains and adjacent regions (QMAR), generating a daily 30 m binary snow cover product over an extensive mountainous region (536,018 km2) from September 2013 to August 2025. Validation against independent Landsat 8 observations yielded an F1-score (FS) of 0.873 and Cohen’s kappa (CK) of 0.859, while Bias values close to unity indicated negligible systematic bias in snow-cover representation. Consistent results obtained from independent Landsat 9 observations and time-lapse photography further supported the validity of the reconstruction, although site-specific evaluation revealed reduced capability for reconstructing short-lived snow events. The reconstructed dataset markedly outperforms the corresponding coarse-resolution baseline while providing enhanced spatial details. Compared with machine-learning models that exclude SCOF-related predictors, the proposed framework yields notable improvements, increasing FS and CK by 4.1% and 4.6%, respectively. Long-term snow persistence provides unique information unavailable from daily MODIS observations alone and is essential for resolving hillslope-scale snow heterogeneity. This study advances hillslope-scale daily snow cover mapping and potentially contributes to improved hydrological modeling and snow hazard assessment in complex mountainous environments.

title: A semi-empirical BPDF model for improving characterization of polarimetric reflection of land surfaces: Validation using laboratory and POLDER polarization data
Editorial Board
Extent and dynamics of tropical flooded forests with multi-year SAR composites and altimetry
abstract: Flood dynamics regulate greenhouse gas emissions from tropical flooded forests, but monitoring flooding beneath dense canopies is challenging. We introduce a L-band SAR approach that uses more than a decade of ALOS-2 PALSAR-2 observations to detect sub-canopy flooding at 100 m resolution across the Amazon and Congo rainforests. We generate multi-year composites of HH and HV backscatter that represent low-, intermediate-, and high-water stages. These hydrological stages are defined locally using over 7000 satellite altimetry time series, accounting for the large variability in the timings of high-water conditions across both rainforests. Flooded forests display a characteristic dual-polarization signature: HV backscatter is comparable to that of non-flooded forests, while HH backscatter is higher due to double-bounce scattering. Quantifying deviations in the HH-HV space, we determine the extent of flooded forests at high-water stage and estimate their seasonal dynamics using a discrete stage-count metric, informing on the number of hydrological stages at which a pixel is classified as flooded forest. Multi-year compositing reduces speckle noise relative to single scenes, enabling the detection of narrow floodplains, while the local definition of high-water conditions improves the representation of high-water conditions across the two rainforests. We estimate approximately 827,000 km 2 of flooded forests under typical high-water conditions, ~687,000 km 2 in the Amazon and ~ 140,000 km 2 in the Congo rainforest. In the Amazon basin, agreement with estimates from Hess et al. (2015), Rosenqvist et al. (2020) and Fleischmann et al. (2022) varies spatially, with high agreement in wide floodplains (e.g., Solimões and Purus rivers), lower agreement along narrower floodplains, and substantial discrepancies in sparsely vegetated areas, partly explained by differences in forest definitions. In the Cuvette Centrale, our estimates show spatial consistency with the estimated extent of peat swamp forests by Crezee et al. (2022), although our flooded forest extent is more spatially restricted. We also found a good correlation between our stage-count map and the microtopography of the Solimões floodplain. By resolving both the extent and seasonal dynamics of flooded forests at 100 m resolution, these maps can support ecological, hydrological, and carbon studies in tropical forests.

title: Quantile-based homogeneity selection and similarity-weighted robust coherence matrix for distributed scatterer interferometry in mining deformation monitoring
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Coal mining can lead to a series of geological issues, making it crucial to monitor surface deformation for early hazard warning in mining areas. Distributed Scatterer Interferometry (DSI) enables the monitoring of deformation in overlying strata above mining working faces. However, the accuracy of this technology is often affected by spatiotemporal decorrelation, necessitating phase recovery processing. The Phase Linking (PL) algorithm can effectively recover the interferometric phase, but it is limited by the correctness of statistical homogeneous pixel selection (SHPs) and the utilization of spatial dimensional information, making it difficult to obtain a sample complex coherence matrix (SCCM) that closely resembles the true situation. This severely impacts the accuracy of the PL estimation results. To address this, this paper proposes two solutions: (1) For SHPs, the medcouple (MC) method is used as a robust measure of skewed distributions, adjusting the boxplot to optimize homogeneous samples in the intensity map, removing outliers and enhancing sample robustness; (2) For SCCM construction, a similarity measure between reference pixels and homogeneous pixels is used as a weight, and a weighted sum with constraint processing is applied to obtain a robust coherence matrix. Simulation and real-world results show that the proposed method can recover phase information severely affected by noise, maintain phase stability, and significantly increase the monitoring point density; its high reliability has been validated through leveling data verification.

title: Design for Machinability: Topology Optimization for Subtractive Machining Using Trimmed Neural Fields
abstract: Topology optimization has found significant utility in additive manufacturing, but the resulting geometries are often difficult to realize using subtractive methods. The complex, curved surfaces of optimized designs typically require time-consuming point milling operations. In contrast, geometries composed of developable surfaces are well suited to flank milling, enabling substantial improvements in machining efficiency and surface quality. However, globally minimizing Gaussian curvature leads to overly simplistic designs. We address this challenge with a novel method that represents geometry using three implicit neural fields, optimized to produce machinable components. The resulting designs consist of regions of developable surfaces separated by seamlines where curvature is concentrated. Seamlines are efficiently computed as intersections of the implicit fields, while the geometry emerges through their product. By constraining surfaces to align with the cutter’s normal or tangential direction, our approach further accommodates practical constraints of 3-axis machining. We demonstrate concurrent optimization of topology and Gaussian curvature, enabling control over seamline feature scale. Compared to methods that enforce subtractive machinability without considering milling efficiency, our approach consistently reduces machining time while maintaining competitive structural performance.

title: Methodology for assessing the accuracy of long-term, annual land cover monitoring at national scale: Experiences from the Land Change Monitoring, Assessment, and Projection (LCMAP) initiative
abstract: Annual land cover monitoring using medium-resolution satellite imagery represents a transition from periodic mapping campaigns to continuous observation systems. This transition introduces accuracy assessment challenges not encountered in one-time mapping efforts, particularly when the initial monitoring period is extended forward in time. These challenges are not addressed in existing guidance, which remains largely framed around the evaluation of maps of a single date or maps showing changes between two dates. We present a set of methodological adaptations to adjust to this evolving paradigm, using as a case study the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) Land Change Monitoring, Assessment, and Projection (LCMAP) initiative, which generated annual land cover and land cover change products across the historical Landsat archive. Assessing the accuracy of these products was an essential component of LCMAP and resulted in an extensive reference sample dataset that may be used for accuracy estimation, area estimation, or support in the development of new algorithms or models. We review the LCMAP methodology and highlight challenges encountered and lessons learned that are transferable to other long-term, temporally dense monitoring programs. This framework demonstrates that statistically rigorous assessment can scale to operational annual land cover production, while the experiences of the project clarify where existing good practice guidance should be extended to support the needs of ongoing, continuous land cover monitoring.

title: SAMWater: a prompt-guided multimodal framework for transferable water mapping with the segment anything model
abstract: Accurate and transferable surface water mapping is critical for water resource assessment, flood monitoring, and aquatic ecosystem management, but remains difficult because SAR speckle, optical contamination, heterogeneous backgrounds, and scarce high-quality pixel-level annotations limit robust large-scale mapping. We propose SAMWater, a prompt-guided multimodal framework that integrates Sentinel-1 SAR, Sentinel-2 optical imagery, the Segment Anything Model (SAM), and Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM 3). Instead of using SAR and optical data as independent classifiers, SAMWater transforms their complementary information into structured prompts for coarse-to-refined water segmentation. A physically interpretable multisensor coarse water prior is first generated from Sentinel observations using an automatic threshold-based strategy. This prior is then refined through prompt-based boundary refinement, a multi-prompt excavation strategy that derives point, box, and Gaussian-style mask prompts, and Water-IoU fine-tuning for water-specific candidate ranking. Using globally distributed samples and manually interpreted PlanetScope reference labels, SAMWater achieved average Kappa coefficients of 90.71%, 85.63%, and 89.05% in evaluations stratified by water body type, land cover background, and climatic zone, respectively. It generally outperformed traditional thresholding and clustering methods, public deep learning models, and existing global water or land cover products, particularly in structurally complex river, reservoir, urban, agricultural, and mountainous scenes. Ablation experiments confirmed that multimodal prior fusion, structured prompt construction, and water-specific ranking jointly drive the performance gains. Moreover, SAMWater-generated refined labels improved the training of U-Net, DeepLabV3+, and SegFormer, indicating their utility for weakly supervised segmentation. SAMWater therefore demonstrates that integrating physically interpretable remote sensing priors with promptable foundation models provides a practical pathway for transferable surface water mapping, large-scale multisensor weak-label generation, and more consistent monitoring of surface water extent.

title: Comparison of NASA Harmonized Landsat and Sentinel-2 (HLS) surface reflectance products with MODIS NBAR
abstract: Frequent surface reflectance measurements at fine spatial resolutions are crucial for land surface monitoring. The NASA Harmonized Landsat and Sentinel-2 (HLS) project addresses this need by combining data from Landsat and Sentinel-2 missions to provide 30-m surface reflectance products with a global average revisit frequency of 2-3 days. This study evaluates the consistency of the HLS Version 2 (V2.0) product against the established Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) Nadir Bidirectional Reflectance Distribution Function-Adjusted Reflectance (NBAR) dataset. We found a high degree of consistency between HLS and MODIS NBAR, with strong positive correlations across all six common spectral bands (R 2 values: 0.939–0.986). Globally, mean absolute differences (MADs) were generally low, typically under 0.03 for visible bands and below 0.05 for NIR and SWIR bands. However, we observed band-dependent discrepancies, with higher discrepancies in the blue and SWIR1 bands. Spatially, substantial differences were found in polar regions, largely due to isolated snow, ice, and water which are fractional and hard to detect within the coarser MODIS pixels but are filtered out in the HLS data. This finding suggests a potential explanation for past disagreements in vegetation trend analyses involving the use of satellite data of different spatial resolutions, as coarser-resolution datasets may mischaracterize greening trends in areas with partial snow and ice cover. These insights are vital for helping users interpret HLS data more effectively and for refining multi-sensor data fusion methods. Our research also provides a valuable baseline for ongoing quality assessment of the HLS product for applications such as vegetation monitoring, land management, and disaster response.

title: Tracking vegetation disturbance, recovery, and sustainability in open-pit mining areas of Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei Region from 2000 to 2024
abstract: Evaluating the overarching efficacy of mine greening initiatives and supporting land resource management within open-pit mining areas requires accurate long-term monitoring of both vegetative degradation and its subsequent regenerative phases. Overcoming the bottlenecks of conventional methods in decoupling vegetation abrupt disturbances from gradual recovery processes, this research utilizes the Google Earth Engine (GEE) and Landsat data spanning from 2000 to 2024. The investigation explicitly targets open-pit mining areas across the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei region. Through the synergistic integration of the Continuous Change Detection and Classification (CCDC) and an adaptively refined NDVImed,t segmentation baseline, we extracted the spatiotemporal dynamics of abrupt vegetation disturbance and gradual recovery events. Furthermore, to rigorously quantify the enduring stability and long-term persistence of these vegetation dynamic trajectories, the study coupled the non-parametric Sen–MK trend estimator with calculations of the Hurst exponent. The results demonstrate that the F1 score for detecting disturbance and recovery events over the past 25 years stably exceeded 0.8, exhibiting excellent temporal robustness. The derived chronological trajectories pinpoint 2013 as a significant turning point for vegetation dynamics. Before this critical juncture, the landscape suffered from intense degradation, marked by an average annual vegetative deficit of 962.19 ha. In the post-2013 era, a recovery-dominated paradigm emerged, characterized by an average yearly restoration of 831.37 ha. Crucially, the aggregate intensity of this vegetation greenness reached 1.64, substantially overshadowing the historical extraction-induced disturbance magnitude of 1.23. Concurrently, evaluations of trajectory persistence reveal that while a substantial 36.56% of the monitored landscape is undergoing sustained ecological enhancement, whereas 22.46% was characterized by persistent deterioration. Precipitation and temperature showed a limited influence on vegetation dynamics (R2 = 0.0796, p = 0.402), while enterprise consolidation and reclamation policies were the main drivers for post-2013 recovery. The acquired quantitative remote sensing evidence not only reveals the core role of macro-policy regulation in driving the reshaping of surface landscapes in mining areas but also provides solid scientific support for the future refined ecological governance of regional territorial space.
