title: A review of remote sensing for agricultural drought: technologies, indices, modelling advances and future prospects
abstract: Agricultural drought is a complex hazard that jeopardises food security and progress toward the Sustainable Development Goals. We systematically reviewed peer-reviewed English-language literature published between 2015 and 2025, focusing on Remote Sensing (RS)-driven agricultural drought monitoring and prediction. Eligible studies were identified from the Web of Science and Scopus databases (last searched in August 2025); review articles, duplicates, and irrelevant studies were excluded, resulting in 181 articles. This review critically examined the evolution of sensors, drought indices, modelling approaches, and emerging technologies used to assess agricultural drought across diverse agro-ecological regions. Specifically, we (1) systematically evaluated the use of optical, thermal, and microwave RS platforms, along with satellite-based, model-based, and reanalysis products for agricultural drought monitoring; (2) reviewed widely used RS-based drought indices, including single indices grouped into nine categories, as well as composite indices; (3) reviewed software or programming languages applied; (4) assessed the progression of modelling approaches from traditional statistical and time-series methods to machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) frameworks; and (5) examined validation strategies applied to agricultural drought assessment. The analysis reveals a growing research interest in this topic, with a strong geographic concentration in Asia, particularly China. Optical and thermal platforms (e.g. MODIS and Landsat) dominate the literature (~54%) due to their accessibility, followed by satellite-derived precipitation products (17%), while microwave soil-moisture missions remain underutilized (~7%). Regarding RS-based indices, most studies employed more than one index: 44% analysed multiple individual indices, 51% used composite indices (either alone or in combination with individual indices), and only 5% relied on a single index. Vegetation indices, such as NDVI, remain workhorses; however, their sensitivity to soil background effects and canopy saturation has driven increased adoption of thermal composites (e.g. VHI), as well as adaptive weighting schemes and principal component analysis-based approaches. Moreover, computational tools used in drought research can be broadly grouped into geospatial and RS platforms for large-scale data processing and analysis (e.g. QGIS, GEE), and general-purpose programming languages (e.g. R, Python) for model development and advanced analytics. Regarding the methodology, statistical and time-series approaches account for 64% of the reviewed studies, followed by ML models (20%) and DL methods (15%), while explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) remains nascent. Techniques, such as random forests, support vector machines, and CNN and LSTM architectures, generally outperform traditional models but require large training datasets and raise concerns related to interpretability and ethics. In terms of validation, hydro-climatic indices such as SPI and SPEI are most commonly used (32%), followed by crop yield and yield anomaly data (19%). This review further identifies key research gaps across sensors, indices, and modelling approaches and proposes a roadmap for developing equitable, interpretable, and resilient agricultural drought monitoring systems. Emerging opportunities include context-aware and interpretable AI, multi-sensor and multi-scale data fusion across optical, thermal, and microwave domains, integration of physiologically meaningful indicators such as sun-induced chlorophyll fluorescence (SIF), robust uncertainty quantification, and the development of hybrid and physics-informed modelling frameworks.

title: Effectiveness of multi-source merged soil moisture products using different triple collocation methods: A comprehensive assessment incorporating spatial similarity evaluation framework
Integrated retrieval of ocean surface wind and current fields from single-geometry SAR observations through a physically constrained Bayesian framework
Mapping subsurface combustion cavities in underground coal fires using nonlocal DS-InSAR and physics-based inversion
The conditional nature of error estimates in multi-source satellite SIF cross-evaluation: How product combinations, statistical models, spatial scales, and temporal treatments shape the conclusions
An optimized methane retrieval approach based on morphological fusion for mapping methane point emissions from spaceborne imaging spectrometry
VLM-Mapper: Multimodal vision-language models for prior guided lane-level HD map construction
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: The automated construction of High-Definition (HD) maps from remote sensing data is essential for modern intelligent transportation systems and spatial data infrastructure. While imagery provides a scalable solution for lane-level HD map construction, traditional discriminative models often struggle in complex scenarios because of their reliance on local visual features and limited use of external geographic context. To address these limitations, this paper introduces VLM-Mapper, a framework that reframes lane-level HD map construction as a multimodal sequence-generation task based on visual–language alignment and prior-conditioned token generation. VLM-Mapper systematically integrates high-resolution aerial imagery with tokenized geographic prior prompts, including standard map metadata and boundary entry points, to guide HD map construction. Furthermore, to mitigate the spatial inconsistencies and count errors of autoregressive decoding, we implement a two-stage post-training pipeline. This strategy establishes spatial alignment via Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT), followed by a Reinforcement Learning (RL) phase using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with a custom geometry-aware and numerical reward function. Experimental results on the large-scale OpenSatMap dataset show that VLM-Mapper achieves state-of-the-art performance and improves the robustness and topological consistency of HD map construction across large-scale aerial imagery.

title: GGFA-SwinIR: A gradient-guided and frequency-aware joint multi-scale framework for bathymetric DEM super-resolution
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: High-resolution bathymetric digital elevation models (DEMs) support marine geoscience, but global grids can smooth fine-scale terrain where observations are sparse. We present GGFA-SwinIR (Gradient-Guided Frequency-Aware SwinIR), a shared-backbone discrete multi-scale framework for × 2 , × 4 , and × 8 reference-grid reconstruction. The framework integrates gradient-magnitude guidance, bicubic-base residual prediction, and pixel, gradient, and complex-spectrum supervision. Under bicubic degradation of GEBCO_2025, GGFA-SwinIR achieved H-RMSE values of 5.13, 9.82, and 18.90 m and PSNR values of 70.28, 65.48, and 59.84 dB at × 2 , × 4 , and × 8 , respectively. In a four-severity low-pass diagnostic, GGFA-SwinIR achieved the lowest H-RMSE and highest PSNR among six methods in all 12 severity-scale conditions and the lowest slope-angle RMSE in 11. Cross-product transfer comparisons with GMRT v4.3 showed the lowest H-RMSE across two evaluation regions and three scales. These results demonstrate the value of jointly modelling terrain gradients and spectral structure for multi-scale bathymetric reference-grid reconstruction and provide an empirically validated basis for exploratory grid enhancement.

title: WMoE-Net: wavelet-directed cross-attention alignment with mixture-of-experts network for multimodal SAR-optical ship detection
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Multisource remote-sensing fusion benefits port and near-shore ship surveillance: optical images provide rich textures in daylight, while SAR remains informative in day-and-night and all-weather conditions. Yet high-resolution SAR–optical ship detection is challenged by scarce near-simultaneous acquisitions, residual misalignment after co-registration, and condition-dependent modality degradation. We curate MSOSD-1.0, a high-resolution paired SAR–optical dataset for port/near-shore ship detection, containing 1,715 co-registered patch pairs with 17,915 oriented ship instances and diverse conditions (low illumination, clouds/fog, cluttered backgrounds). On this basis, we propose WMoE-Net, a correspondence-constrained and reliability-aware alignment–gating–fusion framework. A wavelet-directed cross-attention module (WCAM) enhances local correspondence under residual mismatch. A condition-informed quality gating network (CIQGN) performs sparse expert routing among optical-preferred, SAR-preferred, and collaborative-fusion branches, while a mutually-guided consistency-aware fusion expert (MCFM) refines the collaborative branch to enhance fusion quality. Experiments on MSOSD-1.0 and QXS-SAROPT-SHIP show consistent gains over strong single-modal and multimodal baselines, especially under low illumination and clouds/fog.

title: Beyond accuracy: environment-dependent performance and threshold robustness of spectral water indices across regions and seasons
abstract: Spectral water indices are widely used for operational surface-water mapping, yet large-scale automation is often hindered by threshold uncertainty and limited cross-scene transferability. Existing studies typically rank indices by peak accuracy while overlooking the critical trade-off between maximal performance and sensitivity to threshold perturbations. Here we establish a broad multi-region, multi-season benchmark using Sentinel-2 imagery, covering 12 environmentally heterogeneous regions and four seasons (48 scenes). Twelve representative indices are assessed in terms of scene-adaptive peak accuracy (F1max) and threshold robustness, quantified by a newly proposed Robustness Smoothness Index (RSI). We also introduce PCA-Bridge, which embeds scenes using environmental variables only and maps performance and robustness landscapes in the resulting environmental space. Rather than identifying a single universal index, our analysis reveals a clear trade-off between peak accuracy and threshold robustness. While a median F1max>0.92 across 48 scenes suggests generally high performance, performance declines markedly in complex environments, particularly those dominated by snow and ice. NDWI attains high peak accuracy (F1max≥0.95) in 50.0% of scenes but shows low robustness (RSI≥0.75 RSI≥0.75 RSI≥0.75 in only 8.3%), indicating strong threshold sensitivity. By comparison, MBWI and AWEInsh achieve the highest median F1max (0.968 and 0.960), whereas WI2015 and NWI exhibit the strongest robustness overall, with the nhighest mean RSI (0.840 and 0.837) and broad robustness coverage (RSI≥0.75 RSI≥0.75 RSI≥0.75 in 87.5% of scenes). These findings support task-oriented index selection rather than one-size-fits-all ranking. Out-of-scene transfer experiments showed that scene-wise optimal performance does not guarantee threshold generalisation. Overall, the proposed framework helps identify when peak accuracy, robustness, and transfer performance align or diverge, supporting more reliable large-scale surface-water monitoring.

title: Unlock the Benefits
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence

title: PGD-Net: Prompt-Guided Hybrid Transformer Decoder for building extraction from remote sensing images
abstract: Accurate building extraction from remote sensing imagery is essential for urban planning, cadastral mapping, and geographic information updating. However, existing methods still struggle with semantic degradation during feature decoding, small-building detection, and accurate boundary delineation. To address these issues, we propose PGD-Net, which integrates feature-conditioned prompt guidance into the decoding process for building extraction. The proposed method introduces learnable internal feature prompts to compensate for degraded building semantics. These prompts are further integrated into a hybrid Transformer decoding framework to guide feature reconstruction. Furthermore, a two-level optimization strategy is adopted: TOAM enhances small-building feature responses at the feature level, while a lightweight morphological post-processing step is applied at the output level to refine predicted masks and alleviate boundary discontinuities. Experiments were conducted on three public benchmark datasets, including Massachusetts, WHU, and Inria, as well as the newly constructed Xiamen Building Dataset (XM). PGD-Net achieved IoU scores of 76.81%, 92.05%, and 84.18% on the Massachusetts, WHU, and Inria datasets, respectively. It also delivered the best performance on the XM dataset, which contains a large number of dense urban village buildings with severe occlusions and shadows. The results demonstrate that PGD-Net effectively improves extraction completeness, boundary accuracy, and small-building detection performance in complex urban environments. The code is available at https://github.com/dawnlight129/PGD-Net.

title: RSFF: a reconciliation-sparse fusion framework for semantic segmentation of rocky desertification land in multimodal time series
abstract: Accurate identification of rocky desertification land (RDL) is crucial for ecological environment monitoring and management in karst regions. However, RDL extraction is often hindered by land-cover confusion, seasonal variability, and the fragmented, small, and irregular spatial distribution, when existing methods insufficiently exploit multi-temporal multimodal information. To address this issue, we construct the first dual-modal RDL semantic segmentation dataset with time series (RD dataset) and propose a reconciliation-sparse fusion framework (RSFF) for multi-temporal multimodal data. The framework adopts a dual-branch encoding architecture with multilevel spatio-temporal interaction to separately extract spatial and temporal features from optical and Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imageries. Through the designed Convolutional Attention Reconciliation Module (CARM), multidimensional enhanced features are reconciled, and the Sparse Cross Fusion Module (SCFM) is employed to improve feature discriminability while reducing computational complexity compared with conventional dense attention mechanisms, enabling deep complementarity of cross-modal information. Experimental results on the RD dataset demonstrate that RSFF can effectively distinguish RDL from similar land-cover types, such as bare land and cropland, and significantly enhance RDL boundary delineation while maintaining high classification consistency. The mean intersection over union (mIoU) and overall accuracy (OA) reach 82.94% and 94.28%, respectively, outperforming other state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods. In addition, experiments on the public PASTIS-R dataset further verify the robustness of RSFF under different landscape characteristics and small, fragmented parcel distributions. The RD dataset and code are available at https://github.com/laopiao-lp/RSFF.

title: Seasonal asymmetric changes between photosynthesis and canopy structure phenology across the northern hemisphere
abstract: Vegetation phenology is a critical indicator of terrestrial ecosystem responses to climate change. However, our understanding of the asynchrony between photosynthetic and canopy structural phenology remains limited. Using satellite-derived datasets of gross primary productivity (GPP) and leaf area index (LAI) from 1982 to 2018, we systematically quantify this phenological asynchrony across the Northern Hemisphere (>30°N). At the primary 50% relative-amplitude threshold, GPP-derived transition dates preceded the corresponding LAI-derived transition dates by 7.02 d in spring and 17.51 d in autumn on average, although spring offsets were more spatially variable. During the study period, ΔSOS had a trend of −0.584 d decade−1, indicating a widening spring lead of the GPP-derived transition. By contrast, ΔEOS had a trend of + 0.643 d decade−1, indicating a narrowing autumn offset. Boosted regression tree models identified spring temperature as the climate variable most strongly associated with spring asynchrony, whereas autumn asynchrony showed comparable associations with autumn temperature and solar radiation. Our findings provide phenological evidence for a seasonally asymmetric and shifting structure-function relationship in northern terrestrial ecosystems under climate change. Accounting for the asynchrony between photosynthetic and canopy structural phenology is thus essential for advancing satellite-based vegetation monitoring and carbon cycle modelling.

title: High-resolution Antarctic sea surface temperatures from Landsat enabled by cloud-native processing and novel seal-tag validation
Underwater topographic mapping using a fusion of Airborne LiDAR bathymetry and multibeam Echo sounding
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Accurate measurement of underwater topography is of significant importance for maritime affairs, marine resource development, and environmental protection. Airborne LiDAR Bathymetry (ALB) can efficiently acquire integrated above-water and underwater data in shallow water areas, while the Multibeam Echo-sounding System (MBES) can precisely measure underwater topography in deep water areas and some shallow water regions. By integrating underwater acoustic and optical data, an integrated above-water and underwater topographic representation can be achieved. However, due to differences in measurement ranges, point cloud accuracy, and density, existing fusion algorithms perform poorly in combining ALB and MBES point clouds. This paper proposes a point cloud fusion method suitable for ALB and MBES data. The proposed method first uses a virtual grid combined with the alpha shape algorithm to quickly determine the overlapping area and removes edge triangles using boundary points, reducing the influence of edge triangles. Then, to minimize the impact of topographic differences on coarse point cloud registration, a point-to-plane ICP (Iterative Closest Point) algorithm based on TIN (Triangulated Irregular Network) grid vertex cutting planes is applied, with weighting assigned to the points corresponding to the matching cutting plane’s grid vertices. To mitigate the impact of point cloud density, the distance loss term in the Non-Rigid ICP cost function is changed from a point-to-point distance loss term to a point-to-plane distance loss term. The root mean square error (RMSE) in three experimental regions decreased from 0.149 m, 0.185 m, and 0.217 m to 0.038 m, 0.035 m, and 0.078 m. For comparative analysis, classical Non-Rigid ICP and TrICP (Trimmed Iterative Closest Point) algorithms are implemented using the same preprocessing procedures. The results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves better performance than both the Non-Rigid ICP and TrICP approaches in terms of geometric consistency. These results demonstrate the advantages of the proposed method in terms of both accuracy and robustness when applied to complex scenarios.

title: How does hillside urban expansion affect the surface urban heat island effect? empirical evidence from China
abstract: Global urbanization has driven the expansion of urban construction land into high-altitude areas. This hillside urban expansion (HUE) reshapes the underlying surface pattern and profoundly affects the formation and evolution of the surface urban heat island (SUHI) effect. However, the underlying mechanism by which HUE affects the SUHI effect has not been systematically elucidated. Based on multi-source remote sensing data from 2001 to 2023, this study constructed an urban climbing intensity comprehensive index (CICI) and an SUHI intensity index, and analyzed the spatio-temporal differentiation characteristics of HUE and the SUHI effect at the provincial, municipal, and county scales in China. A structural equation model, an interpretable random forest model, the optimal parameter geographical detector, and the geographical pattern causality model were then applied to reveal the mechanisms by which HUE affects the SUHI effect across the four quadrants demarcated by the Heihe–Tengchong Line and the Bole–Taipei Line (clockwise from Northeast China). The main findings are as follows: (1) The dynamic process of HUE at different scales was dominated by low-intensity expansion; the center of gravity of the static slope ratio was consistently located in the second quadrant (South and Southwest China), with its overall movement trajectory perpendicular to the Heihe–Tengchong Line during the study period. The proportion of medium- and high-intensity slope-climbing cities increased slowly, and high-intensity slope-climbing cities were mostly distributed in the second quadrant. (2) The distribution of SUHI intensity showed scale similarity and regional heterogeneity from 2001 to 2023. The combined proportion of cities with cold islands and strong heat islands remained stable at approximately 60%, and the spatial scope of the SUHI effect generally exhibited an expansion trend characterized by “widespread dispersion and localized clustering.” (3) Natural environmental and human activity factors jointly shaped the driving pathways of the SUHI effect. The cumulative contribution of key influencing factors such as built-up height, the kernel normalized difference vegetation index, annual average temperature, and nighttime light intensity reached 76.4%, exhibiting significant temporal heterogeneity and spatial nonlinearity. (4) The effect of HUE on the SUHI effect followed a cascade process of “direct driving—interaction enhancement—threshold constraint—pathway transmission.” No statistically stable HUE intensity threshold was identified at the national scale, whereas in the second quadrant, two independent methods consistently indicated that the marginal warming effect of HUE tends to saturate once its intensity exceeds 0.27. This study proposes differentiated policy recommendations, providing an important reference for mitigating the thermal effects of HUE and promoting sustainable urban development.

title: Automated camera parameters estimation and occlusion-aware visibility mapping of urban CCTV using asynchronously acquired MMS LiDAR
abstract: Pre-installed urban CCTV cameras form a dense, city-wide sensing network with significant potential for urban geospatial monitoring. However, most deployed units lack accurate camera parameters including position, orientation, and Field of View (FoV) geometry, which prevents their systematic integration into urban geospatial information systems. This study presents a fully automated pipeline that estimates these parameters and produces occlusion-aware visibility polygons as Geographic Information System (GIS) vector outputs from asynchronously acquired Mobile Mapping System (MMS) Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) point clouds. The pipeline needs no on-site access, no physical calibration targets, and no prior knowledge of the camera’s interior orientation, viewing direction, or lens distortion. The only positional input is an approximate horizontal camera location, such as that recorded in a municipal camera inventory or measured with consumer-grade GNSS. A coarse-to-fine strategy bridges the radiometric and temporal gaps between the LiDAR data and the optical imagery. Installation heights are inferred from the geometric signature of the pole in the point cloud, the approximate viewing direction is found by intensity-image matching on rendered panoramas, and precise 2D-3D correspondences are then established by deep feature matching with multi-stage spatial filtering. Camera parameters (interior orientation, exterior orientation, and radial distortion) are jointly estimated with a photogrammetric projection model that requires no initial approximations. An occlusion-aware visibility module then casts 3D rays against the full point cloud to separate ground that the camera can actually see from ground hidden by buildings and vegetation, and the boundaries are exported as GIS-ready vector polygons. Experiments on 21 urban CCTV cameras give a mean 3D camera position error of 0.85 m (σ = 0.33 m) despite a six-month gap between the MMS survey and the CCTV imagery. The resulting visibility polygons reach a mean Intersection over Union (IoU) of 0.721 against manually delineated ground truth. On the common 20-camera subset used for the manual baseline, the proposed method reduces the mean 3D position error by 81.2% (0.87 m versus 4.62 m) and is more accurate for 19 of the 20 cameras, supporting its reliability for large-scale deployment.

title: Towards continental-scale SWOT-based modeling of reservoir operations
abstract: The advent of reservoir models has enabled the monitoring and prediction of reservoir operations (inflow, storage, and release); however, the in situ operation data used for model parameterization is spatially scarce. In this study, we evaluate reservoir monitoring capabilities by leveraging observations from multiple satellite missions to reconstruct reservoir operations, optimize reservoir model parameters, and simulate operations. For reservoirs in the US and Brazil, we design a set of experiments relying on different combinations of in situ , satellite, and hydrologically modeled data sources as reservoir model inputs to characterize the error of satellite- and model-informed reservoir operations. We also make the first attempt to evaluate the use of the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) satellite mission data record for reservoir optimization and simulation. Our results show that simulated storages (median nRMSE ≤ 0.30–0.50; represents maximum across experiments for each country and altimetry dataset) perform significantly better across all experiments than simulated releases (median nRMSE ≤ 0.68–0.94). Accuracy of simulated releases is strongly dependent on the quality of the inflow time series: using in situ inflow (median KGE = 0.56–0.68) for reservoir modeling has greater accuracy than hydrologically modeled inflow (median KGE = −0.19–0.15). However, when simulating operations based on altimetry and modeled inflow, 42–67% of reservoirs improve in release KGE compared to simulations without reservoir operations. Overall, our study demonstrates the potential of SWOT and other satellite altimeters for continental-scale reservoir storage monitoring, and that improving inflow simulations is crucial for release monitoring.

title: Estimation of rice leaf angle distribution from geometric features in millimetric-resolution UAV RGB imagery acquired at 45° viewing angle
abstract: Leaf angle distribution (LAD) is a fundamental determinant of canopy light interception and photosynthetic efficiency, yet its robust quantification remains a major bottleneck. Traditional methods are constrained by either labor-intensive manual measurements or the ill-posed nature of indirect gap probability inversion. Recent advances in deep learning have demonstrated great potential for directly extracting canopy traits from high-resolution imagery. However, whether 2D RGB imagery contains sufficient information to retrieve LAD, a three-dimensional canopy structural trait, is still questionable. We investigated this question by developing a deep learning framework that establishes the relationship between image-derived features and LAD from millimetric-resolution RGB images taken from a UAV. We focused on rice crops representing one of the main cultivated species. A total of 332 rice plants were digitized to construct realistic 3D canopies; we generated 21,600 paired images and GT LAD labels via physically based rendering. In silico experiments demonstrated that deep learning models enable efficient LAD estimation, particularly when taking images inclined at 45° perpendicularly to the rows. Further, our model achieved substantially higher accuracy for average inclination angle (AIA, R 2 = 0.608, RMSE = 1.590°) compared to gap probability-based inversion (R 2 = −0.788, RMSE = 3.397°). Finally, our model showed superior performance from the transplanting to booting stage (R 2 avg > 0.94 for LAD) when applied to actual observations. Application to over 1000 cultivars across two years confirmed high repeatability, establishing a scalable solution for large-scale monitoring. Interpretability analyses, supported by feature visualization and ablation studies, reveal that the model explicitly extracts geometric features specific to leaf inclination, while disentangling them from confounding canopy variables in millimetric-resolution RGB imagery. This feature-level discrimination underpins the model's superior accuracy and ensures robust generalization in diverse field scenarios.

title: Surface-to-volume physics-informed model for 3D mesoscale eddy detection: Multi-source multi-scale fusion
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Mesoscale eddies play a crucial role in the ocean, and accurate detection of their three-dimensional (3D) structures is essential for understanding marine dynamics. However, 3D eddy reconstruction remains challenging: traditional methods provide limited pixel-level boundary delineation, while existing deep learning approaches suffer from insufficient physical constraints and unrealistic eddy geometries. To address this issue, we propose a surface-to-volume physics-informed model (StV-PI-EddyNet) for extracting 3D mesoscale eddies. We construct a high-quality 3D eddy dataset covering the North Pacific (100°E–100°W, 5°N–65°N) down to 1000 m for model training. The model takes sea surface height (SSH), sea surface temperature (SST), and surface current components (U/V) as inputs and consists of three core modules: 2D feature extraction, 3D feature inversion, and 3D semantic segmentation. It embeds a vorticity prediction branch for physical constraints and uses U-Net-like architectures with spatial and channel attention mechanisms. The loss function combines weighted Dice loss and a vorticity-driven physical loss (mean square error + gradient consistency loss) to ensure high segmentation accuracy and physical consistency. Experimental results show StV-PI-EddyNet model achieves 96.97% global accuracy, 84.80% weighted Dice coefficient, and 0.8955 macro-averaged F1-score. It effectively mitigates boundary distortion issues of existing methods, generating 3D eddy masks with high spatial precision. This model enjoys good scalability and can be further optimized by integrating earth observation advances in architecture design, data sources and application generalization, promoting its in-depth applications in marine and especially underwater dynamic research.

title: Improved estimation of lake storage variation via DEM reconstruction integrating elevation and morphological constraints
abstract: High-quality Digital Elevation Models (DEMs) are essential for accurately estimating lake storage variations, but the high cost of in-situ measurements limits their large-scale application. Reconstructing DEMs from remote sensing-derived lake contours is a promising low-cost alternative. However, most existing methods primarily rely on elevation-matched contours and discard those without elevation data. Consequently, the loss of morphological constraints leads to incorrect topographic structures and significantly amplifies reconstruction errors where elevation data are sparse. To overcome this limitation, we proposed a valued and Non-valued contour–based Unified DEM reconstruction model (NUDEM), which integrates contours with elevations and those without elevations to exploit both elevation constraints and morphological constraints. Evaluated on four lakes in the Tibetan Plateau, NUDEM consistently outperformed five existing methods in DEM reconstruction, reducing the RMSE by approximately 60% compared to the second-best method, with an average RMSE of 0.93 m and a minimum RMSE of 0.15 m. For lake storage variation estimation, NUDEM improved R2 by about 30% over other DEM-based methods and nearly doubled the R2 of traditional hypsometric-curve-based methods. This method provides a low-cost, remote sensing-based solution for large-scale lake DEM reconstruction, offering significant potential for improving the accuracy of lake storage variation estimation.

title: Spatiotemporal characteristics of vegetation responses to compound drought and heatwave events in Central Asia
abstract: With climate warming intensifying, compound drought and heatwave (CDHW) events have become more frequent and intense in arid Central Asia, severely affecting vegetation growth. However, systematic quantitative assessments of vegetation responses and their drivers under such compound extremes remain limited. Using meteorological and remote sensing data, we identified growing-season CDHW events across Central Asia from 1982 to 2023. Integrating the Kernel normalized difference vegetation index (KNDVI) and the long-term continuous SIF-informed photosynthesis proxy (LCSPP), we established a vegetation response indicator system including total loss (LOSStot), maximum decline (DECmax), and time to decline (TIMEdec) to characterize vegetation damage. We further applied the XGBoost model and SHAP analysis to quantify the environmental driving effects and interactions. The results indicate that CDHW events increased significantly during 1982–2023, with heatwave frequency rising at 0.38 days yr−1 and an abrupt shift around 1996. High-frequency CDHW events were primarily concentrated in north-central Kazakhstan and northern Xinjiang, China, while their frequency and duration generally increased with latitude, indicating a pronounced northward enhancement pattern. CDHW caused larger vegetation losses than individual drought or heatwave events. Event duration was the most important environmental variable of LOSStot, with the highest mean SHAP value (0.140), while precipitation anomalies during events showed a strong association with rapid vegetation decline, with a direct path coefficient of 0.333 for DECmax. This study clarifies vegetation loss characteristics and key contributing factors under compound extremes in Central Asia, providing a scientific basis for ecological risk assessment and climate adaptation in arid regions.

title: Single-scene thin-cloud correction for dynamic macroalgal blooms via water-referenced radiative transfer
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Thin clouds substantially attenuate spectral signals in satellite imagery, leading to systematic underestimation of macroalgal bloom coverage. Existing thin-cloud correction methods have critical limitations for dynamically drifting blooms: they typically require paired cloudy-clear observations or stable surface conditions, which are rarely available, or inadequately account for cloud-induced attenuation, particularly in the near-infrared band that is essential for algal quantification. This study proposes a single-scene thin-cloud correction framework for dynamic macroalgal blooms that removes both additive scattering and multiplicative attenuation from visible to NIR bands. By exploiting local atmospheric consistency between algal patches and adjacent water, the method infers localized cloud effects from neighboring water pixels. Cloud-free and cloud-affected water pixels are first identified to estimate clear-sky and cloudy top-of-atmosphere reflectance. A linear conversion model derived from radiative transfer theory then relates these two reflectances through coefficients C T and C R , whose relationship is constrained by a MODTRAN-based lookup table (LUT). The coefficients are solved by combining the conversion model with a quadratic polynomial relationship between C T and C R established from the LUT. Validation using GaoFen‑1 and Landsat‑8 imagery against near-concurrent Sentinel‑2 observations over the Southern Yellow Sea demonstrates effective near-infrared restoration. Using two complementary validation strategies—macroalgal area estimation from real images and reflectance evaluation from simulated cloudy data—the proposed method achieves consistently higher accuracy than representative state‑of‑the‑art methods. Application to golden tide events in the East China Sea further confirms its robustness and transferability. The method provides a practical, physics-guided solution for monitoring dynamic macroalgal blooms under thin-clouds contamination.

title: Satellite-based coastal monitoring through variance image composites (SatVar)
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: The past decade has seen rapid advancements in satellite remote sensing data availability and analysis. In coastal environments, this has enabled regional to global assessments of shoreline trends, a key practical application for management and planning. However, coastal zones are inherently dynamic, while instantaneous shorelines only capture the state of the system at a particular moment in time. This study introduces a novel approach for monitoring dynamic coastal environments using satellite imagery, adapting the principle from ground-based video monitoring systems. The SatVar approach presented here uses freely available, medium resolution satellite imagery and Google Earth Engine. The method takes advantage of the increasing availability of cost-free Sentinel-2 imagery and the flexibility of collections acquired over different time periods to automatically detect highly dynamic zones through variance composites, image compositing and segmentation to obtain medium-term trends of coastal dynamics. Natural boundaries are rarely abrupt, so a zone-based (instead of a line-based) approach provides more nuanced information about transitional zones. The identified highly dynamic zones correspond to morphological processes described in literature, and are also used for shoreline extraction. This combined information can enrich understanding of coastal dynamics and overcome some of the limitations of instantaneous shorelines. The approach is tested at three locations with different morphodynamic characteristics and tidal regimes: Sancti Petri (Spain, mesotidal), Narrabeen (Australia, microtidal) and Sefton (UK, macrotidal). Potential applications to monitor changes outside the upper shoreface such as coastal dune dynamics or back-barrier environments are also discussed.

title: Robust hyperspectral retrieval of mangrove functional traits across species and spatial scales using GA-ELM
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Plant functional traits provide critical indicators of ecosystem functioning, biodiversity maintenance, and plant adaptive strategies under environmental change. However, hyperspectral retrieval of mangrove functional traits remains challenging because trait-related spectral signals are strongly influenced by species composition, canopy structural heterogeneity, and intertidal background effects, leading to unstable trait-spectrum relationships across species and scales. To address these limitations, this study developed a genetic algorithm-optimized extreme learning machine (GA-ELM) framework for robust retrieval of mangrove functional traits under heterogeneous mangrove spectral conditions. Three key traits, including chlorophyll content (Cab), equivalent water thickness (EWT), and leaf mass per area (LMA), were retrieved for four dominant mangrove species using leaf-level hyperspectral measurements and canopy-scale GF-5 imagery. GA-ELM generally outperformed PLSR, RF, and conventional ELM in species-specific comparisons. Leave-one-species-out validation yielded R 2 ranges of 0.61–0.75 for Cab, 0.60–0.72 for EWT, and 0.66–0.76 for LMA, indicating moderate predictive capability for previously unseen species, with performance varying among species and traits. At the canopy scale, GA-ELM achieved stable estimation accuracy for Cab, EWT, and LMA based on GF-5 imagery ( R 2 > 0.75), demonstrating that the framework can be independently calibrated for canopy-scale retrieval. Independent cross-regional validation yielded R 2 values of 0.60, 0.49, and 0.44 for Cab, EWT, and LMA, respectively, indicating moderate but reduced cross-regional transferability. Spectral sensitivity and band-selection analyses revealed species- and trait-dependent patterns that provided context for interpreting variation in predictive performance. These results remain conditional on one GF-5 acquisition per site and 30 m mixed-pixel conditions, and broader tidal-stage and cross-sensor validation is still required. These findings demonstrate the potential of GA-ELM for hyperspectral retrieval and spatial mapping of mangrove functional traits.

title: Spaceborne multi-sensor tracking reveals hydrologic decoupling during the record-breaking Sahara flood
abstract: Satellite remote sensing enables large-scale quantification of extreme hydrologic events in data-scarce regions, yet the integration of multi-sensor observations to resolve hydrologic responses remains limited. The record-breaking 2024 Sahara flood presents a unique opportunity to evaluate satellite-based characterisation of hydrologic extremes in hyper-arid environments. By integrating multi-sensor satellite observations of precipitation, surface inundation, and terrestrial water storage, we provide a comprehensive assessment of this event’s hydrologic scope. Intense rainfall, delivering annual precipitation totals within just a few days, triggered widespread flooding, with the 2024 inundation extent estimated to show an approximate cross-sensor increase of 38 ± 9% relative to the historical GLAD/Landsat benchmark (1999–2023), reaching up to a 40-fold increase in some basins. Concurrently, regional terrestrial water storage exhibited an unprecedented surge, with its intra-annual amplitude doubling the long-term average. However, this hydrologic response was spatially variable. In the eastern basins, surface inundation and terrestrial water storage increased concurrently, indicating strong hydrologic coupling. In contrast, several western basins exhibited pronounced surface flooding but comparatively weak TWS responses, revealing a decoupling between flood magnitude and basin-scale storage response. These findings highlight the capability of multi-sensor satellite observations to resolve spatially heterogeneous hydrologic responses and reveal the non-stationarity in the conversion of flood hazards into terrestrial water storage gains in hyper-arid environments. This study provides a transferable approach for monitoring hydrologic extremes in ungauged regions.

title: A scene-mapped framework for deriving clear-sky surface longwave downward radiation from remotely sensed measurements
Assessing plant area index and 3D plant area distribution in wheat canopies from a terrestrial LiDAR system for high-throughput plant phenotyping
abstract: This study investigates a new methodology to estimate plant area index ( PAI ) and its spatial distribution from 3D point clouds acquired by a system of 3 LiDARs (2 nadir-viewing and one at 45°) mounted on the Phenomobile Unmanned Ground Vehicle designed for high-throughput phenotyping of herbaceous crops. It relies on the computation of the gap fraction at the voxel level using the trajectories of the laser beams to numerically invert the Beer-Lambert law (BL), enabling the simultaneous estimation of PAI and AIA (Average Inclination Angle, in°). The method is evaluated on wheat crops both in silico (i.e. simulations based on the AdelWheat functional structural crop model coupled with a point cloud simulator) and in actual phenotyping trials of a panel of 10 bread wheat genotypes grown in two study sites under different treatments of plant density, water stress and sowing dates. The in silico validation indicates that the numeric inversion of BL with the LiDAR system of the Phenomobile leads to a relative error of 9.8% (RMSE = 0.32, R 2 = 0.99) and 8.4% (RMSE =5.4°, R 2 = 0.95) in the estimation of PAI and AIA , respectively. The validation in actual phenotyping experiments against destructive measurements produced satisfactory results for canopy PAI (RMSE = 1.44, R 2 = 0.82), while requiring prior knowledge on AIA , e.g. either by (i) introducing a regularization term in the cost function used to invert BL, to avoid unexpected high AIA estimations, (ii) using a fixed, reference value of 60°. The analysis of the results indicates that the inclusion of a regularization term mitigates the impact of actual differences in leaf inclination among cultivars on PAI accuracy, while providing a relative description of the actual variability in the vertical profile of leaf inclination across the different cultivars.

title: Hydroclimatic signatures of flash drought heterogeneity and rice-yield responses in China
abstract: Flash drought poses a growing threat to agricultural production because its rapid onset limits timely monitoring and adaptive management. Using ERA5-Land root-zone soil moisture, this study identified flash drought events across China from 2004 to 2023, characterized their spatiotemporal patterns and hydroclimatic associations, assessed cross-product consistency of the identified onset signals, and examined their associations with rice-yield anomalies. GLEAM root-zone soil moisture was used for cross-product onset-consistency assessment, and a spatially validated Random Forest–GeoShapley framework was applied to examine the hydroclimatic associations of flash drought duration, severity, and intensity. Flash droughts occurred more frequently in southern and southwestern China, whereas longer and more severe events were concentrated in northern arid, plateau, and high-latitude regions. GLEAM showed consistent root-zone soil-moisture depletion around ERA5-Land-identified onset dates, supporting the timing and direction of the identified onset signals. GeoShapley analysis indicated that geographic background accounted for a substantial share of the total contribution. Precipitation deficit contributed most strongly to duration and severity, whereas intensity showed a more distributed contribution from precipitation deficit and atmospheric-demand variables. April–September drought exposure was generally associated with lower rice-yield anomalies, with flash drought showing more negative exposure–response estimates than slow drought, particularly in the Northeast China Plain. These findings clarify attribute-specific hydroclimatic associations of flash drought and support region-specific monitoring and rice-production risk assessment in China.

title: Stage-integrated fire resilience assessment of forest vegetation and its driving factors
abstract: Forest vegetation responses to fire intensities remain insufficiently understood, particularly across the successive stages of resistance and post-fire recovery. To address this issue, we selected 771 independent fire events that occurred between 2005 and 2020 in representative conifer-dominated forests of Northeast China, including larch-, pine-, and spruce-dominated vegetation communities. The fire month was defined as the disturbance onset, and each fire event was examined over a 97-month observation period comprising 48 months before and 48 months after the fire. Forest fires were classified into normal- and high-intensity groups, and a three-stage analytical framework was developed to link pre-fire vegetation health, resistance during fire disturbance, and post-fire recovery. Using historical burned-area records and a Transformer-based counterfactual model, we reconstructed fire-free trajectories of the Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI), solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence (SIF), and Net Primary Productivity (NPP). These indicators were subsequently integrated through tensor decomposition to construct a Composite Resilience Index (CRI). Because these air and soil temperatures were naturally varying environmental factors rather than experimentally controlled variables, their effects were statistically accounted for as time-varying covariates in the modeling and driver-attribution analyses. Cumulative resistance was consistently higher than instantaneous resistance, indicating that vegetation partially compensated for its initial fire-induced losses over time. NPP exhibited the greatest short-term stability, whereas SIF showed the strongest immediate sensitivity to fire disturbance. Under high-intensity fire, the fitted recovery-deviation transition points occurred at 9.5 months for EVI, 10.5 months for SIF, and 36.5 months for NPP. These values indicate that the recovery trajectory of ecosystem productivity changed substantially later than those of vegetation structure and photosynthetic functioning. The CRI was significantly lower at 12, 24, and 48 months following high-intensity fire, indicating a persistent multidimensional resilience deficit rather than a short-lived reduction immediately after the fire. SHAP analysis further identified monthly air and soil temperatures as the dominant environmental predictors of post-fire resilience. These findings provide a multidimensional basis for forest fire-risk assessment, vegetation vulnerability evaluation, and stage-specific restoration management in high-latitude forest ecosystems.

title: RTAS: A radiative transfer model for agricultural strip-intercropping structures
Improving regional winter wheat yield estimation by assimilating cross-scale heterogeneity information from UAV and satellite remote sensing
Corrigendum to “Reference-anchored envelope modelling for predicting tree mortality hotspots driven by drought” [Int. J. Appl. Earth Observ. Geoinform. 154 (2026) 105609]
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Global asymmetric mangrove-edge shifts reveal coastal squeeze under sea-level rise
abstract: Changes at the land–sea interface reveal whether mangrove systems advance seaward, retreat landward, or undergo coastal squeeze as their seaward and landward boundaries converge. Yet global assessments have largely relied on area change, with less focus on these directional processes. This study applies a global coastline-normal transect framework to Global Mangrove Watch data for 1996, 2008, and 2020. By quantifying the seaward and landward edges together with width and centroid position, we distinguish expansion, directional migration, and contraction across multiple spatial scales. Globally, mangroves lost an average width of 77.2 m: the seaward edge retreated landward by 47.5 m, a pattern consistent with marine forcing including relative sea-level rise and coastal erosion, while the landward edge shifted seaward by 53.7 m, compatible with restricted accommodation space. Together, these opposing movements reveal widespread asymmetric contraction. Among regions exhibiting clear directional migration, 65.2% shifted seaward, including advances of up to 2.5 km in Marajó Bay, Brazil, whereas less frequent landward migration reached 5.6 km in the northern Gulf of Mexico. After 2008, the prevalence of landward migration increased, particularly across Asia and Africa. The edge trajectories constrain the set of plausible controls but do not uniquely attribute change to sea-level rise, sediment supply, topography, land use, or restoration. Conservation should therefore protect potential landward migration pathways while accounting for uncertainty in the mechanisms producing individual local trajectories.

title: Multi-task learning for simultaneous surface water and burned area mapping from earth observation data
abstract: Multi-task learning has emerged as a promising approach for combining related tasks into a unified framework with reduced computational costs through shared representations. However, its application to hazard mapping using Earth Observation data remains underexplored. In this study, we provide the first systematic evaluation of multi-task deep learning architectures for simultaneous detection of crisis information (surface water and burned area) using Sentinel-2 and Landsat-8 optical imagerytwo societally critical hazards with strong operational demand for rapid and accurate detection. We evaluate five semantic segmentation architectures: three U-Net variants with different encoders (MobileNetV2, EfficientNet-B4, ResNet50) and two transformer-based SegFormer models (SegFormer-B0, SegFormer-B4). Each architecture was trained in both single-task learning and multi-task learning modes. For reference data, we employed the benchmark S1S2-Water dataset for water body detection and constructed a novel burned area dataset by integrating diverse global datasets with already available in-house annotations. Both reference datasets cover heterogeneous geographic regions and temporal periods. The results show that multi-task learning effectiveness is highly architecture-dependent. Burned area detection achieved F1-scores ranging from 0.624 to 0.701, with three of five architectures showing improvements under multi-task learning. SegFormer-B4 reached the best performance (F1-score: 0.67) with gains of +8.24% over its single-task baseline, while EfficientNet-B4 achieved the highest absolute accuracy (F1-score: 0.701). Conversely, ResNet50 exhibited negative transfer with an F1-score decrease of 8.24%, demonstrating that not all architectures benefit from multi-task learning. Water detection performance remained consistently high across all models (F1-score > 0.97), with SegFormer-B4 achieving an F1-score of 0.98. Importantly, the multi-task framework reduces inference time by 89–91% and parameter count by 17–48% compared to maintaining two separate single-task models, demonstrating its practical value for operational emergency mapping services where rapid hazard assessment is critical.

title: Privacy Leakage on DNNs: A Survey of Model Inversion Attacks and Defenses
HR-INR: Continuous Space-Time Video Super-Resolution via Event Camera
abstract: Abstract Continuous space-time video super-resolution (C-STVSR) aims to simultaneously enhance video resolution and frame rate at an arbitrary scale. Recently, implicit neural representation (INR) has been applied to video restoration, representing videos as implicit fields that can be decoded at an arbitrary scale. However, existing INR-based C-STVSR methods typically rely on only two frames as input, leading to insufficient inter-frame motion information. Consequently, they struggle to capture fast, complex motion and long-term dependencies (spanning more than three frames), hindering their performance in dynamic scenes. In this paper, we propose a novel C-STVSR framework, named HR-INR, which captures both h olistic dependencies and r egional motions based on INR. It is assisted by an event camera – a novel sensor renowned for its high temporal resolution and low latency. To fully utilize the rich temporal information from events, we design a feature extraction consisting of (1) a regional event feature extractor – taking events as inputs via the proposed event temporal pyramid representation to capture the regional nonlinear motion and (2) a holistic event-frame feature extractor for long-term dependence and continuity motion. We then propose a novel INR-based decoder with spatiotemporal embeddings to capture long-term dependencies with a larger temporal perception field. We validate the effectiveness and generalization of our method on four datasets (both simulated and real data), showing the superiority of our method. The project page is available at https://github.com/yunfanLu/HR-INR .

title: Efficient Test-Time Prompt Tuning for Vision-Language Models
SLCA++: Unleash the Power of Sequential Fine-Tuning for Continual Learning with Pre-training
DreamMix: Decoupling Object Attributes for Enhanced Editability in Customized Image Inpainting
CLIDD: Cross-Layer Independent Deformable Description for Efficient and Discriminative Local Feature Representation
Blurring Modal Boundaries: A Unified Survey from Single- to Multi-modal Person Re-ldentification
Semantic Privacy Protection with Utility Preservation for 3D Point Clouds
abstract: Abstract Point cloud data face serious semantic privacy risks during acquisition, transmission, and cross-institutional sharing. Existing methods mostly rely on geometric perturbation or destructive encryption, which can reduce the recognizability of the original class but often impair downstream usability. This paper proposes a class-transfer-based semantic encryption framework for point clouds, aiming to conceal original class information while preserving task utility and supporting authorized recovery. Specifically, we construct a unified latent space with a shared-backbone Normalizing Flow, and combine LoRA and FiLM to achieve parameter-efficient class-conditional adaptation. We further introduce diffusion-guided flow alignment to regularize the latent distribution, construct an energy-based category transition graph, and obtain an optimal class-transfer table through global matching. Then, a latent-space Neural ODE continuously evolves source-class latents into target-class latents, which are decoded into target-class point clouds through the inverse flow. We adopt attacker-oriented metrics, including New-Class Recognition Rate (NCRR), Original-Class Leakage Rate (OCLR), and Original Label Recovery Rate (OLRR), to evaluate privacy and utility. Experiments on classification and segmentation benchmarks show that the proposed method achieves controllable semantic transformation, effectively reduces original-class semantic leakage, preserves downstream learnability in the protected domain, and supports reliable authorized reconstruction.

DOME: A Decoupled Offline-Online Memory Externalization Framework for Interpretable Domain-Generalized Face Anti-spoofing
A novel framework for urban–rural gradient classification by integrating multidimensional urbanization features via self-supervised learning
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Rapid urbanization has transformed vast natural landscapes into increasingly complex human-dominated environments, giving rise to pronounced urban–rural gradients. However, accurate classification of such gradients remains challenging because biophysical indicators alone cannot fully represent the socioeconomic heterogeneity embedded in the urban–rural continuum. Here, based on multisource Earth observation and geospatial datasets, we propose a novel urban–rural gradient classification framework that integrates multidimensional urbanization features, including, land development, population density, economic intensity, and social vitality, to establish a five-class urban–rural gradient classification scheme-Urban core, Urban area, Suburban area, Rural area, and Natural area. Then, we developed URGCNet, a spatial clustering-driven self-supervised learning model that incorporates ordinal constraints to capture the ordered structure of the urban–rural continuum. Based on this framework, we produced URGCdataset, a 500 m urban–rural gradient classification dataset for mainland China for five benchmark years (2005, 2010, 2015, 2020, and 2025). The framework achieved strong classification performance, with URGCNet reaching an overall accuracy of 91.0% and URGCdataset reaching 93.6% against an independent test sample dataset. Ablation experiments show that removing individual urbanization features reduced the Kappa coefficient by 0.1–0.2, highlighting the indispensable role of socioeconomic information beyond biophysical indicators. Spatiotemporal analysis reveals a clear expansion of human-activity areas over the 2005–2025 period, during which the share of natural areas decreased from 92.7% to 90.0%. Overall, this framework provides a transferable pathway for establishing comparable urban–rural gradient classifications across diverse regional contexts and offers a new spatial foundation for urban environmental and ecological applications.

title: A framework for inversion and assimilation of deep-sea mirror ocean acoustic tomography observations
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: The deep ocean plays a critical role in the global climate system. However, satellite Earth observation is limited to the sea surface, while in-situ measurements struggle to achieve synchronous coverage over vast oceanic areas. Ocean Acoustic Tomography (OAT) is an essential method for retrieving large-scale interior ocean parameters; however, its path-integral nature leads to high-dimensional and ill-posed inverse problems when applied to the deep ocean. To address this, this paper develops a unified modular framework for the inversion and assimilation of acoustic remote sensing data, specifically designed for Mirror OAT (MOAT) in the deep sea. Through a configurable dimensionality reduction representation, the framework regularizes the ill-posed inverse problem in a low-dimensional space, enabling a stable and efficient numerical solution. High-resolution ocean model-based simulation experiments are conducted to evaluate its performance. Results show that the inversion module reconstructs 3-D flow fields via a “section-to-plane” two-step method, with inversion errors below 0.15 m/s over most of the water column relative to the true fields from the high-resolution ocean model. The assimilation module integrates observations using an Ensemble Kalman Filter based on a low-dimensional subspace, improving the analysis field accuracy by approximately 35 % compared to the background field. Further sensitivity experiments indicate that the assimilation method exhibits superior robustness against observation noise, while the inversion method offers higher computational efficiency by requiring neither an ensemble of model forecasts nor sequential cycling. Parameter analyses provide a basis for selecting the appropriate approach under different scenarios. This study provides a complete workflow, from methodology to numerical validation, for efficient and accurate estimation of deep-sea interior states from MOAT observations. It may serve as a reference for the design and operational application of deep-sea 3-D remote sensing observation systems.

title: Image-projected apparent particle size distribution estimation in rock avalanches using direct deep regression from UAV imagery
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Due to the rapid downslope movement of fragmented rock masses, rock avalanches are among the most destructive geomorphic hazards in mountainous regions. Particle size characteristics observed at the surface provide useful information for interpreting fragmentation, transport, and depositional patterns. Recent advances in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based remote sensing and deep learning have enabled novel methodologies for PSD estimation. However, achieving rapid acquisition and reliable PSD characterization under complex field conditions remains challenging. To address these challenges, we constructed and preprocessed a dedicated UAV dataset for PSD analysis from high-resolution RGB imagery acquired with a DJI Matrice 300 RTK platform. Based on this dataset, we proposed a direct deep regression pipeline to predict characteristic image-projected apparent PSD descriptors, including D 20 , D 40 , D 60 , D 80 , and D max , directly from UAV image patches. The proposed approach was compared with two baseline methods: handcrafted feature-based regression and semantic segmentation-based contour pipelines. Experimental results showed that the direct deep regression pipeline achieved better overall PSD prediction performance than the baseline approaches, with ConvNeXt-Tiny obtaining the lowest mean absolute error (MAE) of 2.23 cm and resolution-normalized MAE of 16.77 ground sampling distance (GSD) units. The model exhibited more stable predictive performance for the intermediate percentiles (D 40 –D 80 ), whereas relatively higher errors were observed for D 20 and D max . The trained model was applied to representative areas within the study deposit to generate spatial maps of surface-visible apparent PSD, demonstrating its potential for UAV-based characterization of surface particle size patterns in fragmented rock deposits. Additional transfer validation on tunnel boring machine (TBM)-excavated rock images provides preliminary evidence of cross-scenario transferability across different material and imaging conditions. True cross-event validation on independent rock avalanche deposits remains to be conducted.

title: Integrated remote sensing and geotechnical investigations of the 2022 Jiujiawan mudstone landslide in Xining city, China: from deformation monitoring to failure mechanisms
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Mudstone landslides are widespread worldwide, with their initiation and evolution mainly governed by the coupled effects of rock mass microstructure and hydromechanical behavior. However, the linkage between Earth observation (EO)-derived deformation signals and microscale weakening mechanisms remains poorly constrained. Using the catastrophic Jiujiawan landslide (15 September 2022, Xining, China) as a case study, this research aims to reconstruct the spatiotemporal evolution of the landslide and explain the multiscale mechanisms connecting microscale material degradation with macroscale slope failure through evidence-based interpretation. To achieve this, an integrated framework combining multisource EO data, geotechnical investigations, and laboratory analyses was applied. This approach clarifies deformation characteristics and failure mechanisms from coupled macro- and microscale perspectives. At the macroscopic scale, a high-fidelity three-dimensional model was reconstructed using unmanned aerial vehicle photogrammetry. Satellite optical imagery was used to qualitatively trace the pre-failure evolutionary trajectory, complemented by interferometric synthetic aperture radar to quantitatively reconstruct spatiotemporal displacement sequences. At the microscopic scale, X-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy, and energy dispersive spectroscopy characterized the mineralogical suite and microstructural fabric. These analyses reveal the properties of Paleogene mudstone intercalated with gypsum layers, showing how pore-fracture networks accelerate rock mass degradation. Synthesis of the results indicates a process-based linkage whereby microscale hydromechanical weakening (clay mineral hydration, argillization, and gypsum dissolution) is progressively manifested as macroscopic creep and acceleration in EO-derived displacement time series, with seismic preconditioning (the 2022 Ms 6.9 Menyuan earthquake) further reducing the slope’s structural threshold through mechanical fatigue, ultimately leading to slope failure under extreme precipitation. This transferable multiscale framework supports mechanism-informed hazard assessment and enables EO‑based early detection and staged early warning for clay‑rich, water‑sensitive slopes that undergo progressive creep under hydromechanical coupling, especially during extreme climatic events.

title: A method for identifying urban flood inundation based on single-temporal remote sensing imagery
abstract: Rapid mapping of urban flood inundation is critical for emergency response and decision-making. However, existing methods often rely heavily on multi-temporal data or deep learning models, limiting their timeliness and computational efficiency. This study proposes an automated method for mapping urban flood inundation from a single post-event image acquired by the Sentinel-2 Multispectral Instrument. The method adopts a three-stage framework comprising spectral-index-based segmentation, morphological-feature-based separation, and spatial-topological assessment. It was evaluated using three flood events in Zhengzhou, China; Manville, United States; and Porto Alegre, Brazil. Independent validation yielded overall accuracies of 0.9985, 0.9371, and 0.8834; precision values of 0.6719, 0.6771, and 0.8229; and F1-scores of 0.8037, 0.7001, and 0.7615, respectively. The extracted flood extents were further compared with those obtained using two conventional approaches and were generally consistent across the three study areas. Agreement F1-scores ranged from 0.694 to 0.870 relative to pre- and post-flood change detection based on the modified normalised difference water index, and from 0.603 to 0.866 relative to newly inundated area extraction using the European Commission Joint Research Centre permanent surface-water mask. On an experimental platform equipped with an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin, processing the Porto Alegre, Manville, and Zhengzhou scenes required 24.3, 2.68, and 19.8 s, respectively. These quantitative results indicate that the proposed method can identify major urban flood inundation areas under diverse geographical and hydrological conditions. Requiring only a single post-event multispectral image, no model training, and no high-performance computing, the method provides a lightweight solution for rapid urban flood inundation mapping and resource-constrained applications, including onboard satellite processing.

title: Detection of soil moisture variations beneath an asphalt layer using L-band SAR
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR)-based soil moisture retrieval has primarily focused on bare or vegetated surfaces, whereas asphalt generally considered a highly attenuating medium that limits the detection of subsurface soil. Here, we used an L-band SAR sensor in a microwave anechoic chamber to characterize the detectable depth through asphalt and its controlling factors, and further quantitatively investigate the responses of interferometric phase, coherence, and closure phase to infiltration-induced variations in subsurface soil moisture. Results show subsurface echoes remain detectable through at least 9 cm of asphalt using an L-band Mini-SAR, while modeling indicates that increasing transmit power and antenna aperture could extend detectable depth beyond 30 cm. The InSAR observables exhibited distinct responses to infiltration-induced subsurface moisture variations. The mean interferometric phase decreased linearly with increasing soil volumetric water content (VWC) ( r = - 0.992 ), with an average phase shift of approximately 0.53° per 1 % increase in VWC. Spatial analysis further revealed a strong correspondence between regions of reduced coherence and nonzero closure phase and the infiltration-affected area. Overall, this study provides theoretical and methodological support for improving the subsurface detectability of airborne and vehicle-based L-band SAR sensors and for InSAR-based detection of soil moisture variations beneath asphalt layers.

title: Thinking on maps: how foundation model agents explore, remember, and reason in map environments
abstract: Map environments provide a fundamental medium for representing spatial structure and supporting navigation, planning, and geographic analysis. Understanding how foundation model (FM) agents acquire, consolidate, and utilize spatial knowledge in such environments is therefore critical for enabling reliable map-based reasoning and applications. However, most existing evaluations assess spatial ability in passive and non-interactive settings, without requiring models to actively explore environments, accumulate observations, and progressively construct spatial knowledge. Consequently, how spatial knowledge is formed during exploration and used for reasoning remains poorly understood. In this paper, we propose an interactive evaluation framework to examine how FM agents explore, remember, and reason in symbolic map environments. Agents incrementally navigate partially observable grid-based maps composed of roads, intersections, and points of interest (POIs), receiving only local observations at each step. Spatial understanding is then evaluated through a suite of tasks, including direction judgement, distance estimation, proximity judgement, POI density recognition, and path planning. By systematically varying exploration strategies, memory representations, and reasoning schemes across multiple foundation models, we identify distinct functional roles of these components. Exploration mainly affects experience acquisition but has a limited influence on final reasoning accuracy. In contrast, memory representation plays a central role in consolidating spatial experience, with structured memories—particularly sequential and graph-based forms—substantially improving performance on structure-intensive tasks such as path planning. Reasoning schemes further shape how stored spatial knowledge is utilized, with advanced prompting strategies supporting stronger multi-step inference. We also observe performance saturation across model versions and scales beyond a certain capability threshold, suggesting that further gains in map-based spatial understanding may depend more on spatially specialized representations and reasoning mechanisms than on model scaling alone. Overall, this work advances process-oriented evaluation of spatial cognition in FM agents and offers practical insights for building more reliable map-based reasoning systems.

title: Assessing heat dome effects on forest dynamics in the Pacific Northwest using Planet imagery
abstract: Abstract Increasingly frequent extreme heat events are imposing significant stress on forest ecosystems, with implications for forests and the organisms that live in them. This study evaluates the effects of the June 2021 Pacific Northwest (PNW) heatdome (a prolonged high-pressure system that generated record-breaking temperatures) on forest canopy health and its subsequent recovery within the conifer-dominated Ellsworth Creek Preserve in Washington state, USA, using high-resolution Planet Labs satellite imagery. We analyzed normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) trends from spring to fall from 2017 to 2024 to identify canopy stress and quantify changes in canopy greenness. Experimental forest restoration thinning treatments implemented to test their effectiveness in restoring old-growth forest characteristics at our sites allowed us to assess impacts of the heatdome event relative to these restoration treatments. Our results show a marked decline in summer NDVI following the 2021 heatdome, signaling substantial canopy stress. This decline, different than patterns in the other seven years, was particularly strong in dense, unmanaged (control) forest stands, which exhibited more pronounced NDVI declines than thinned (treatment) stands. These more pronounced stress signals during and after the heat event were associated with greater tree canopy height, canopy complexity, and tree density. The summer NDVI trends over the three post-heatdome years suggest a gradual recovery in tree canopy greenness, with thinned stands showing faster NDVI recovery than controls. In all, these results suggest that restoration thinning may improve canopy resilience to extreme heat. However, recovery trajectories varied widely within stand types, with persistent evidence of stress in high-density areas that suggest incomplete recovery as of 2023. Broadly, these findings show the vulnerability of dense forest canopies to extreme heat events, suggesting that forests with high canopy density may be less adaptable to recurring heat events. Nonetheless, managing forests through restoration thinning may enhance forest resilience to these climate-induced stressors – providing potential guidance for adaptive management strategies to maintain forest health in a world with more extreme climates.

title: Improving automatic glacier mapping accuracy, robustness, and reliability across the Third Pole Region
abstract: Most automatic glacier mapping methods applied in the Third Pole Region (TPR), exhibit suboptimal accuracy for debris-covered glaciers, high sensitivity to interferences, and large uncertainty in model outputs, thereby limiting their operational utility. These challenges can be mitigated by deploying advanced deep learning models and enhancing dataset representativeness across complex imaging conditions. Accordingly, we compiled three large-scale datasets used for model development, glacier-level mapping evaluation, and cross-sensor generalisation assessment, respectively. We then evaluated several state-of-the-art deep learning networks and found that the adapted TransUNet performed best. On the test dataset, the model achieves a glacier Intersection over Union (IoU) of 90% and 83% in patches featuring debris-free and debris-covered glaciers, respectively, while maintaining robust under challenging conditions. Glacier-level validation further confirms the effective detection of glacier counts and precise outlines, with both metrics improving with glacier area and the global IoUTPR > 80%. Uncertainty quantification shows high output reliability, with expected calibration errors of 0.029 and 0.009 for the test and glacier-level test datasets, respectively. Our fully automated 2024–2025 Karakoram glacier inventory, comprising 12,981 glaciers covering a total area of ~19,484 km2, exhibits high agreement with earlier inventories and reflects current glacier state. The primary contribution of this study is the development of a scalable framework that, by optimising dataset representativeness and algorithmic architectures, significantly elevates the accuracy, robustness, reliability and operational value of glacier mapping across the TPR.
